desc: Crown-appointed governors are installed across our Italian holdings, keeping a firm grip over the towns and cities of the peninsula and leaving little room for local defiance.
policies.name: Direct Rule

desc: Italian communes and nobles are left to govern their own affairs. Freed from the burden of central oversight, cities invest in themselves and grow rich in the process.
policies.name: Local Autonomy

desc: Italian lands are put to work for the crown. Their workshops run harder and their levies are called more freely, funneling the output of the peninsula into our coffers and armies.
policies.name: Tribute System

desc: The crown expands its administrative reach by issuing new ordinances for its Italian holdings, creating offices to extend royal authority and tightening the king's grip over the domain.
policies.name: Ordonnances Royales

desc: Adelantados govern Italian cities in the crown's name, drawing them into Iberian trade networks and pulling them ever closer into the orbit of the realm.
policies.name: Adelantamiento of Italy

desc: Governors from the East are installed across Italian lands, reasserting a foreign power's presence on the peninsula and drawing its peoples gradually into the fold of the realm.
policies.name: Catepanate of Italy

desc: Italian territories are incorporated as imperial fiefs, their populations bound by feudal obligation. The Emperor's presence quiets local discontent while swelling the ranks of imperial levies.
policies.name: Italian Imperial Fiefs

desc: Defines how the crown governs its Italian territories in the wake of the Italian Wars.
entities.name: Administration of Italian Lands

desc: Our state consists of many different smaller states, each with their own customs and laws. All provinces, governed by their own councils, contribute to the central authority and align their policies along common lines.
policies.name: Autonomous Councils

desc: The state is administrated as a single council wherein the members decide the policy of the state. Remote areas of our country will struggle to make their voice heard.
policies.name: Central Council

desc: The state rescinds many of their central powers in favor of local courts, which adapt their own administrations to best suit the needs and ways of the local population.
policies.name: Local Courts

desc: We do not rule directly, but through subjects who swear loyalty to us. Influential members of the Nobility whose fealty can be assured are commanded to advise rulers of our subject nations of our pronouncements, which helps breed and maintain loyalty to the Crown.
policies.name: Feudal Administration

desc: A union of other, autonomous states which are the supreme authorities of their territories. The central government is limited to handling foreign politics, while internal affairs are resolved by the states.
policies.name: Confederal Union

desc: The state is an amalgamation of many different smaller states with their own customs and laws. All states, however, are under the rule of the federal government and as such are subject to federal laws.
policies.name: Federal State

desc: Many people demand to be given a role in the government, but mostly because they want to be rewarded without expending much effort. The idea of absolutism has recently piqued our interest, as adopting it would empower us to dispose of those self-serving parasites and rule alone...
policies.name: Absolute Rulership

desc: The state is administrated as a single entity where the central government is the supreme authority of the nation. The provinces have little to say over the internal politics of the country.
policies.name: Unitary Administration

desc: The ''Pyatina'' is the highest administrative division in Novgorod's government. The republic is divided into five Pyatinas, four of which border the city of Novgorod directly, while the fifth encompasses more distant territories.
policies.name: Pyatina Division

desc: The ''Eyalet'' administration is the primary division of the Beylik of the Ottomans. Every ''eyalet'' is ruled by a pasha, who in turn answers to the central government's Grand Vizier. The central laws of the state do not have to apply to every eyalet, and each pasha is free to incorporate local customs and mores to better rule their people.
policies.name: Eyalet Division

desc: A ''Merindad'' is a geographical-administrative division in the kingdoms of Aragon, Castile, and Navarre. Merindads serve as intermediate administrative bodies between the central authority, the towns, and noble holdings. The head of a Merindad is the Merino, entrusted with administrative and judicial powers over their assigned territory as a representative of the ruler.
policies.name: Merindad Division

desc: This Nahua governance system has evolved beyond its initial structure of hereditary ''tlatoani'' leaders. Provinces are now administered by appointed officials: local stewards called ''calpixque'', and high stewards called ''huecalpixque''. These officials manage the provincial tribute system under the supervision of the ''petlacalcatl'' in the capital. In particularly unruly provinces, military governors known as ''cuauhtlatoani'' may be appointed to maintain control.
policies.name: Calpixque System

desc: The Tongue, or ''Langue'' System, categorizes members and assets based on ethnolinguistic divisions. Each Tongue is further subdivided into Priories, Grand Priories, Bailiwicks, and Commanderies. Each Langue has a designated headquarters, known as an ''auberge'', located in the capital of the Order.
policies.name: Tongues Division

desc: The ''Rajyas'' are the main provinces of the Kingdom of Vijayanagar. These territories are each jointly governed by a military commander and a member of the ruling dynasty. Administration is carried out in the region's native language, which allows these laws to be implemented more effectively.
policies.name: Rajya

desc: Our lands are home to numerous unincorporated tribes and clans who could provide valuable service to the state, if properly integrated into our administrative system. As a class, these ''Palaiyakkarar officials'' would serve as law enforcement, fortification builders, provincial representatives, and military officers. Most importantly, they could mobilize their kinsmen to provide us with a steady supply of capable manpower.
policies.name: Palaiyakkarars

desc:
It is in the best interest of our state to encourage economic productivity, while simultaneously keeping a constant watch over regional economies. However, we have not always been successful in our administrative efforts, as ruling over the economic activities of so many subjects requires significant amounts of both human and material resources.
In order to solve this, we have created the ''zabt'' System, which establishes regular cadastral surveys to measure agricultural land, assess crop productivity, and classify land quality. Based on these surveys, standardized revenue rates are calculated and collected in cash rather than in-kind. This creates predictable, systematic taxation that ensures our state revenue reflects our actual agricultural capacity.
policies.name: Zabt System

desc: The Prónoia System functions as a means of temporarily transferring imperial fiscal rights, such as taxes or income from various sources, to individuals or institutions. Unlike the feudal system prevalent in Europe at the time, Prónoia grants were neither hereditary nor transferable, and ultimate ownership remained with the Emperor. In exchange for these privileges, the system ultimately served the purpose for the head of state to raise an army in times of need, and entailed that the troops had to mostly cover their own expenses.
policies.name: Prónoia System

desc: Under the Komnénian emperors, the informal Prónoia system had been codified into a rigorous instrument of imperial policy. Grants were formally contracted, with each holder obligated to furnish a cavalry contingent proportional to the revenues they received. The Emperor retained the right of revocation, and a reorganised imperial registry tracked every grant and its associated military obligation ensuring that the land revenues of the realm translated directly into mounted levy strength under the crown's direct control.
policies.name: Komnénian Prónoia

desc: Facing an exhausted treasury and the constant pressure of civil war and foreign invasion, the Palaeologan emperors have conceded the irrevocable: Prónoia grants are henceforth hereditary. Noble families who previously served at imperial pleasure now hold their lands as permanent patrimony, bolstering the legitimacy of the dynasty through aristocratic loyalty but at the cost of the military obligations that once gave the system its purpose. The cavalry that the grants were meant to fund must increasingly be hired at the state's own expense.
policies.name: Palaiológian Hereditary Prónoia

desc: Rather than allow the Prónoia governors to strengthen their hold on their lands, the system has been changed so any loopholes that made the title of governor hereditary or transferable can no longer be exploited.
policies.name: Reformed Prónoia System

desc: Led by an ''Adelantado'', the ''Adelantamiento'' is an administrative system developed in Castile by which members of the Nobility are placed as governors over frontier or newly conquered territories, reporting directly to the ruler. Adelantados have broad military, judicial, and administrative authority in these remote regions, and often finance expeditions themselves in exchange for land and expanded governing rights.
policies.name: Adelantamiento System

desc: We have delegated control over local economic affairs and business practices to the Nobility governors in those regions. This should help us greatly expand our trade network.
policies.name: Decentralized Trade Federation

desc: A series of documents denoting the main functions of our government, from coronation ceremony etiquette, to the daily activities of the Crown, to the maintenance of our army. This framework serves as a robust basis for our government and the privy council known as ''savaziro''.
policies.name: Regulations of the Royal Court

desc: Equivalent in status to a prime minister, the ''Mahapatih'' has tremendous influence in our political sphere. As the second in command over the entire nation, whoever holds this office is charged with overseeing critical affairs of the state, such as military expansion and the effective operation of the government.
policies.name: Office of the Mahapatih

desc: Any kind of state requires a system to administrate and organize its territory. By selecting an appropriate structure, we can ensure that our authority is enforced in even the most remote parts of our state.
entities.name: Administrative System

desc: Local chiefs and strongmen have great influence over their people. To appease them and win their cooperation would progress our own agenda.
policies.name: Reliance on Local Tribes

desc: While we do not outright recognize their seniority in local matters, maintaining a healthy and respectful relationship between us and local tribes benefits us all.
policies.name: Cordial Relations

desc: The tribal groups that our lands graciously host have sought to disrupt our authority for far too long. If we are to consolidate our grip on power, we must demonstrate our might and bring these unruly factions to heel.
policies.name: Refuse Recognition

desc: The many tribes across our land hold certain authority over local affairs. Our stance towards them may define the course of our history.
entities.name: Amazigh Familial Connections

desc: Some prefer to draw out fights and make them into battles of attrition. This tactic, however, jeopardizes the lives of our warriors. Instead, we should focus on developing superior firepower and annihilating our enemies swiftly.
policies.name: Superior Firepower

desc: We want to maximize the size of our army at all times. This comes at the expense of its quality, however.
policies.name: A Large Standing Army

desc: Our greatest strength does not lie in our offensive capabilities, but in our ability to hold our defenses. Letting enemies wear themselves down by bashing their forces fultilely at our walls will assure our victory.
policies.name: Defensive Stance

desc: It is of great importance that our soldiers reamin disciplined at all times, especially in the chaos of battle. Only through thorough drilling and highly disciplined training can we ensure the survival of our men.
policies.name: Sustained Discipline

desc: Cavalry is the mobile force of our army and serves as shock troops in combat. Our military focuses on increasing its usage, and on integrating cavalry into our regiments.
policies.name: Cavalry Warfare

desc: The wars we lead are not only won on land, but also on the sea. As such, our troops must be prepared to embark as an amphibious unit, ready to strike the coastal defenses of our enemies.
policies.name: Amphibious Specialization

desc: The authority of each captain under our command is undisputed, to such a degree that loyal crews march into gunfire on their orders. Their goal is plunder and legendary adventure; their dreams are fulfilled only uner our unflinching leadership!
policies.name: Authority of the Captain

desc: Army doctrines represent skillsets in which our [

] can specialize. The longer we work under these doctrines, the more entrenched they become in our military culture, and the more skilled we become at them. Over time, this can lead to powerful benefits for our glorious forces.
entities.name: Army Doctrine

desc:
The Peshwa is the prime minister, responsible for the general administration of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Peshwa, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Peshwa Focus

desc:
The Mazumdar is the finance minister, responsible for managing the accounts of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Mazumdar, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Mazumdar Focus

desc:
The Sacheev is the secretary, responsible for the preparation of royal edicts and other policies of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Sacheev, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Sacheev Focus

desc:
The Waqia-Navis is the interior minister, responsible for the intelligence and espionage administration of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Waqia-Navis, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Waqia-Navis Focus

desc:
The Senapati is the commander-in-chief, responsible for the military and the defense of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Senapati, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Senapati Focus

desc:
The Dabir is the foreign minister, responsible for the diplomatic affairs of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Dabir, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Dabir Focus

desc:
The Nyayadhish is the chief justice, responsible for the civil and criminal matters of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Nyayadhish, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Nyayadhish Focus

desc:
The Panditrao is the high priest, responsible for the religious concerns of the state.
The council will grant more power to the Panditrao, increasing their influence in the state.
policies.name: Panditrao Focus

desc: Ashta Pradhan - ''Modern Council of Ministers'' - is the system of ministerial delegation used by the Marathi people. The council is tasked with guiding the administration of the state, overviewing matters of the military, finances, diplomacy, and religion alike.
entities.name: Ashta Pradhan Council

desc: Leadership is no easy position. It requires charisma, valor, and combat knowledge. Fortunately for us, the members of the Nobility are experts in the arts of war, and will lead our forces.
policies.name: Noble Command

desc: The ''Mansabdar'' a military unit wherein Nobility are granted land rights in exchange for performing military and administrative services. Unlike other noble classes, the mansabs are under the direct rule of the ruler.
policies.name: Mansabdari System

desc: Every man who can prove himself as not only a soldier but also as a leader shall have the right to guide our armies to glory. Neither noble nor royal blood plays a role in who can hold this position.
policies.name: Meritocratic Leadership

desc: Despite resistance from the Nobility, we aim to make the army the career of choice for unlanded sons of the aristocracy. We start training them from a young age, which means we not only bind them to us, but we also create a corps of trained noble-born officers for the future.
policies.name: Noble Cadets

desc: The ruler of the state must be also the head of the military. Only then can our soldiers charge at our enemies with the true fearlessness we demand of them!
policies.name: Ruler General

desc: The sailors we employ to run our illicit activities are familiar with our standards and conduct. Therefore, it has become easier for our captains to attract crew for their expeditions.
policies.name: Loyal Privateer Crews

desc: The office of ''Mégas Doméstikos Command'' Great Domestic of the Schools places supreme field command of all imperial armies in the hands of a single appointed commander. Rather than dispersing military authority among competing tagmata officers, the Mégas Doméstikos coordinates strategy across the entire theater of war. The prestige of the office draws the finest Nobles to serve under its banner, and battles won under his banner forge our army into a well tempered one at twice the rate of ordinary campaigns.
policies.name: Mégas Doméstikos Command

desc: An army is only as good as its leadership. An incompetent general can be the bane of their nation, while a military leader of great prowess will be known and feared on every battlefield.
entities.name: Battle Leadership Law

desc: A centralized bureaucracy is anchored in the capital of the kingdom, with most decisions made by or in proximity to the ruler, and then distributed to the provinces.
policies.name: Centralized Offices

desc: A decentralized bureaucracy leaves more decisions to local administrators or governors, who are then answerable to the monarch.
policies.name: Decentralized Offices

desc: The ''namestnik'' is a bureaucratic position comparable to that of a viceroy. They are responsible for the local administration of our provinces and states.
policies.name: Namestnik Office

desc: The Treasury, or ''Rentekammeret'' will administrate our finances and the ''Rentemester'' will answer to the Ruler directly. This allows us better control over our country's finances.
policies.name: Rentekammeret

desc: The merchants in our League enjoy particular privileges afforded by our custody. Despite them being confederated into a loose alliance forged based on mutual interest, they are not constrained by the strings of bureaucracy and red tape.
policies.name: Autonomous Offices

desc: By keeping a record of the traffic across our illicit ports, we can maintain a better grip on the goods and vessels that use our facilities.
policies.name: Port Logs

desc:
In order to best utilize the lands and subjects we control, we must enlarge, reorganize, and professionalize our bureaucracy. We shall create organizations dedicated to administering specific aspects of the state, and thus eliminate the need for ad hoc solutions.

Let us consult with our universities to determine how to most efficiently rule and govern. Meanwhile, we shall encourage our young nobles to serve the state with a pen rather than a sword in hand.
entities.name: Bureaucratic Offices

desc: The Burghers are a powerful entity within our state with strong influence over the economy. Strengthening and reaffirming their rights will bolster their loyalty to our government and protect our economic stability.
policies.name: Strengthen Rights of the Burghers

desc: The merchant families are rapidly growing more powerful. Positions once reserved for the Burghers can now be snatched up by any merchant with a fat purse and enough sway. They must be reminded of their proper place in our society.
policies.name: Curtail the Burghers

desc: Urban life is dominated by the influence of guilds, or groups of Burghers who organize themselves in order to protect national trade concerns and traders. Strengthening the power of these guilds will both obtain their loyalty towards the state, and preserve urban stability.
policies.name: Strong Guilds

desc: The New World is an unimaginable opportunity for many who seek fortune. By granting the Burghers authority over the economic affairs of our colonies, we can keep them busy and away from economic matters in our urban centers.
policies.name: Grant Colonial Authority

desc: We must not allow foreign Burghers to dominate our markets! Increasing our regulatory oversight will curb the influence of foreign merchants and provide a competitive advantage to our own.
policies.name: Increased Trade Regulations

desc: Stifling the flow of commerce from abroad is by no means wise. We should ensure that any potential trading partners feel welcome in our lands in order to safeguard a steady flow of their valuable goods into our markets.
policies.name: Reduced Mercantile Regulations

desc: The position of the Burghers is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Burghers

desc: The Clergy already possess many of the skills we look for in administrators. They are well-educated, experienced scribes, and they have a higher calling. In many ways, allying ourselves with the Clergy would give us access to a skilled cadre of potential administrators.

mods.label: Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Administrative Clergy

desc:
The aristocratic families of the realm must not only provide counsel, but also swear eternal loyalty to our ruler. But as our realm expands, it becomes ever more clear that they must perform service of the spirit as well as of the sword.

It is time for a new generation of Nobility to serve. Shielded by robes and armed with pens, they will fight in service of our state just as their armored brothers do.

mods.label: Possible Nobles in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Nobility of the Robe

desc: We cannot let tradition govern who deserves the privilege of serving our growing nation. Instead, we must look examine the abilties of every candidate. In a meritocratic system, administrators are chosen for their talents, and not for their parentage.

mods.label: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Meritocratic Recruitment

desc: The estates are not trustworthy allies to the Crown, as they will always prioritize expanding their own influence over serving the state. Only the relatives of the ruler should be entrusted with managing our realm's administrative matters.
policies.name: Dynastic Administration

desc: Educated men of lower stature can contribute just as readily as the Clergy, and their practical experience makes them excellent additions to any governmental office. The Yorkist Tradition states that any literate man of notable background may join the ranks of governance, along with those who have devoted themselves to the service of God.

mods.label: Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities
Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Yorkist Tradition

desc: Our cabinet follows the model first adopted and promoted by some of China's most powerful dynasties, sharing the same influences and aiming at being proficient and capable.
policies.name: Sinicized Cabinet

desc: Our pirate republic should be governed by the will of its fiercest captains. It is their alliance that holds our society together, and therefore their judgments should take precedence over any other authority.
policies.name: Council of Captains

desc: The cabinet is the highest office in the government and our ruler's personal advisors. Cabinet ministers and secretaries enjoy special privileges and rights.
entities.name: Cabinet Laws

desc: A follower of the Catholicism faith is able to reduce their time in purgatory with the performance of charity like giving alms or other donations to the instution of the Catholic Church.
policies.name: Cum Postquam

desc: The sale of indulgences is wide-spread and highly commercialized. Followers are able to purchase indulgences directly from members of the Catholic Church, even going so far as purchasing forgiveness for sins not yet commited.
policies.name: Unigenitus Dei Filius

desc: The purchase of indulgences by any means, even the giving of alm, is prohibited.
policies.name: Etsi Dominici Gregis

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church on the matter of Indulgences.
entities.name: The Purchase of Indulgence

desc: No Priest of the Catholic Church is allowed to marry.
policies.name: In Rito Romano

desc: Priests are allowed to marry, but they are not allowed to ascend to a position in the curia.
policies.name: Non in Solo Pane

desc: All priests are allowed to marry.
policies.name: Qualis est Pastor

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church towards the ability of its priests to marry.
entities.name: The Marriage of Priests

desc: The Catholic Church has strong prerogatives and powers over the Catholic Church. The Catholic Church is infallibale.
policies.name: Ultramontanism

desc: Rejecting the total authority of the Catholic Church, Gallicanism places similar importance on the authority of the state.
policies.name: Gallicanism

desc: Conciliarism rejects the total authority of the Catholic Church as a single person, placing it in the hand of an ecumenical council instead.
policies.name: Conciliarism

desc: The Catholic Church is a mere representetive role in the faith, with the authority on questions of faith placed on the ruler of the individual country.
policies.name: Invisible Church

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church on the matter of papal authority.
entities.name: Papal Authority

desc: The presence of Simony is not officially endorsed but tolerated by the Church.
policies.name: Beatior Ist Largitas

desc: Simony is an accepted part of Catholicism doctrine.
policies.name: Quae sunt Caesaris Deo

desc: The practice of Simony is actively presecuted and punished by the Church.
policies.name: Romanum Decet Pontificem

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church on the matter of simony.
entities.name: Simony

desc: The Society of Jesus is not supported by the Catholic Church.
policies.name: Dominus Ac Redemptor Noster

desc: The Society of Jesus is the official representative of the Catholic Church and is allowed to spread the faith with all its might.
policies.name: Regimini Militantis Ecclesiae

desc: The official relations of the Catholic Church towards the Order of the Jesuits.
entities.name: Society of Jesus

desc: The veneration of saints and reliquaries is an essential part of the Catholicism doctrine.
policies.name: Sunt in Regno Dei

desc: While an essential part of Catholicism doctrine, the veneration of saints and reliquaries is restricted to a smaller core of approved objects.
policies.name: Licet ad Colenda

desc: The veneration of saints and reliquaries is prohibited.
policies.name: Ubi Moyses Ascendit

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church on the matter of veneration of saints and reliquaries.
entities.name: Veneration of Saints and Reliquaries

desc: Witchcraft is not acknowledged as real by the Catholic Church.
policies.name: Sicut Malefici Aegyptii

desc: As the ''Malleus Maleficarum'' demands, we need to find and persecute all signs of witchcraft.
policies.name: Summis Desiderantes

desc: The official stance of the Catholic Church on the existance of Witchcraft and other occult practices.
entities.name: Persecution of Witchcraft

desc: Countries will naturally recognize the superiority of the Middle Kingdom and prostrate themselves before the Dragon Throne with their tribute, without the need for rules or regulations to that effect.
policies.name: Free Cèfēng Tǐzhì

desc: A codified, hierarchical tributary system best serves the Middle Kingdom, as it makes it clear which states provide the greatest benefit to the Dragon Throne and therefore deserve commensurate rewards.
policies.name: Codified Cèfēng Tǐzhì

desc: The tributary system has been present in the Middle Kingdom since its inception, as all nations around it dutifully recognize the authority of the Middle Kingdom.
entities.name: Cèfēng Tǐzhì

desc: Free-thinking ideals are both uncontroversial and encouraged. [
] are more likely to settle and remain in a [
] where they can freely express themselves, although there are inevitably zealots who oppose such liberty.
policies.name: No Censorship

desc:
The Clergy has some tolerance for heretical and controversial thinking, but their patience must not be tried.

[
] may leave or refrain from settling in a [
], depending on how their work and peers are treated.
policies.name: Limited Censorship

desc:
There is no tolerance for heretical thinking. The Clergy watches over everything, and will not hesitate to punish those who do not conform.

[
] are less likely to settle or remain in a [
] unless they are adherents of the current religious doctrine.
policies.name: Strict Censorship

desc:
Heresy is not tolerated in any aspect of society, and is punishable by burning at the stake. Religious services, writings, and opinions of a heretical nature will be purged.

[
] are likely to avoid settling or remaining in our country, and religious minorities will see their property confiscated and be subject to persecution.
policies.name: ''De Heretico Comburendo''

desc: The Church is not immune to the purges of the Oprichnina, and members of the Clergy, particularly those who were perceived as a threat, are targeted. Monasteries are regularly pillaged, and monks are subjected to violence. Strict censorship is extended to theological works, religious texts, and historical writings, and people who adhere to different forms of Christianity are viewed with suspicion.
policies.name: Oprichniki Raids Permitted

desc: The Mandate of Ofen will guide our approach to handling the spread of heresy in our country. It will not only dictate what we condemn as heretical, but will also mandate that every parish church must read it aloud to their congregations twice each year to reinforce its statutes among our people.
policies.name: Mandate of Ofen

desc: The ability to control which literary works can be distributed, and whether opinions counter to established dogma are allowed, is essential to religious cohesion and generally favored by the Clergy. However, these restrictions are frowned upon by free thinkers and creative professionals, and can have profound consequences for the availability of [
] and for any [Work of Art] deemed heretical.
entities.name: Censorship

desc: Our patriarchate will integrate this aspect into its core beliefs, embraced by all our members.
policies.name: Allow Christological Debates

desc: Our patriarchate will reject this aspect into its core beliefs, embraced by all our members.
policies.name: Forbid Christological Debates

desc: Debates on the aspect of Christ, our stance towards our brethren sects and our position on the nature of worship are the lifeblood of keeping our belief alive and vibrant!
entities.name: Christological Debates

desc: The thelogical study around the nature of Christ, His identity and the union of his various natures is a delicate art. Many scholars classify Christ as fully divine, thus they subscribe to High Christology, while other adhere to the disciplines of Low Christology.
entities.name: Christology

desc: We will let our provincial governors control the registration process in their own provinces. This may result in a lack of efficiency, but they will feel their authority has been respected.
policies.name: Delegated Civil Registration

desc: The central government authority will take control of the registration process in order to improve efficiency, although the local governors will not like this appropriation of their duties.
policies.name: Centralized Civil Registration

desc: A system aimed at keeping track of all our subjects within our realm as a step towards improving the quality of life for all under our banner.
entities.name: Civil Registration

desc: No embassies can be set anywhere.
policies.name: No Embassies

desc: Clans will be allowed to carry out their own diplomatic actions.
policies.name: Clan Embassies

desc: Diplomatic actions will be carried out at the highest level, following Chinese rules.
policies.name: Allow Chinese Embassies

desc: This law describes how diplomacy will be handled by our people.
entities.name: Clan Diplomacy Law

desc: The various clan leaders have specific posts appointed by the Japanese Shogunate, to whom they own their allegiance. This allows flexibility in how the country is administred.
policies.name: Appointed Posts

desc: The clans have their own domains, to which they have hereditary rights. This will free the bureaucracy of the Japanese Shogunate and allow it to focus on more important tasks, but will also strengthen the power of the clans.
policies.name: Established Domains

desc: The Sankin-kōtai is a system where the vassals of the Japanese Shogunate alternate between the capital and their lands. When in the capital, they are naturally expected to display their wealth, and that financial burden should use up enough of their funds to prevent any mischief.
policies.name: Sankin-kōtai

desc: There should be clear laws defining where the leaders of the different clans must reside, to properly keep the balance of power.
entities.name: Clan Residence

desc: The importance of the Clergy to the masses is undeniable. After all, it is the local cleric who guides the common man directly towards finding divine favor. Guaranteeing rights for our Clergy will win their loyalty, and, by extension, the loyalty of our Commoners.
policies.name: Strengthen Rights of the Clergy

desc: Often enough, the clerical class sees itself as an arbiter for whether state decisions are spiritually and morally correct. They meddle with mundane matters far outside the spiritual world, and as such, their influence must be reduced significantly.
policies.name: Curtail the Clergy

desc: While religion itself is not a problem for us, the extensive rights and influence held by the  Clergy is of great concern for our state and its people. No religious institution shall ever be allowed to intrude on worldly issues. Officially separating the Clergy from the government is therefore necessary.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language

policies.name: Secularization of the State

desc: A senior member of the '''ulamā''' will be given supreme authority to appoint ''Muftī'' and interpret Sharī'ah, and also confirm the new rulers of the realm - but there will be no question that regardless of this, our leader still holds higher authority. This policy can be seen as a compromise that ensures state power, while also enshrining the sanctioned faith's role in state affairs.
policies.name: Šayḵ al-Islām

desc: The position of the Clergy is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Clergy

desc: The metals selected for the coinage of our currency are gold and silver, for two different sets of coins.
policies.name: Gold and Silver Coins

desc: We only use gold as the metal selected for the coinage of our currency.
policies.name: Gold Coins Only

desc: We only use silver as the metal selected for the coinage of our currency.
policies.name: Silver Coins Only

desc: The abundance of copper in Sweden, primarily from the Stora Kopparberget mine in Falun, has prompted the country to use it as the main metal for minting a new national currency, the ''daler''. This is issued as a large money plate, called ''plåtmynt'', which can weigh up to 20 kilograms. Some argue that this might not be very practical and that the volume of money in circulation could exceed copper reserves, but they seem narrow-minded.
policies.name: Swedish Copper Coins

desc: In the sprawling patchwork of our great empire, cooperation and collaboration between neighboring groups is vital to the health of our economy. We shall join the customs union of the Rhine and adopt their ''gulden'' coins to make business transactions less complicated for our merchants, and streamline our international diplomacy.
policies.name: Rheinischer Münzverein

desc: A newly founded organization between cities with a strong Hanseatic presence, the Wendish Coinage Treaty will provide us with a strong basis to facilitate trade and commerce in our lands.
policies.name: Wendischer Münzverein

desc: The metals selected for the coinage of our currency are silver and copper, using different mixtures.
policies.name: Bullion Coins

desc: Different goods and materials, such as livestock, cloth, shells, cacao, etc., may be used as a common currency for trade.
policies.name: Barter Exchange

desc: Derived from a mixture of pure silver and some copper, the Stavraton is meant to replace the defunct ''hyperpyron'' in an attempt to revive the economy and modernize exchange rates.
policies.name: Stavraton Coins

desc: This law determines the resources our country will use to mint its currency. The most common coins are made of gold, silver, and copper, with different mixtures of each material and also different monetary values. However, other exchange systems exist throughout the world that do not depend on this type of currency, but rather on other materials, such as livestock, cloth, shells, cacao, etc.
entities.name: Coinage Law

desc: The principles and methods of the Republic are essential to the freedom of our members and our subjects alike.
policies.name: Found a new Republic

desc: A newfound Monarchy, governing all our members justly, is the only path towards prosperity for.
policies.name: Found a new Monarchy

desc: Neither the free will of the Republican votes nor the authoritarian power of a Monarchy has led our Colonial Federation to independence, but the will of the divine. Only as a unified Theocracy can our people prosper in this world.
policies.name: Found a new Theocracy

desc: With bonds forged in the fires of our struggle for independence, it is time to consider the unification of the loosly bound lands of our members.
entities.name: Unification of the Colonial Federation

desc: We have adopted colonial policies that encourage founding settlements in newly discovered lands, where settlers from the heart of our nation can exploit any [Raw Goods] and continue to expand inland.
policies.name: Settled Colonies

desc: We have adopted colonial policies that encourage the foundation of trading posts and entrepôts in strategic locations, which are aimed at exchanging different goods and opening new [
] for the benefit of our economy.
policies.name: Trade Colonies

desc: We will appoint a regional governor in our name who will be in charge of collecting tribute from the native population of the area. This organization allows us to establish colonies efficiently and with smaller costs than normal, although it is certainly not helping our relationships with the locals.
policies.name: Encomienda System

desc: We have adopted colonial policies in alignment with Sepúlveda's reasoning that native peoples are naturally disposed to be slaves, and that slavery is also the best way for their Christianity overlords to convert them to the true faith. As a result, the landowners in our colonies face no retribution for the way they treat the local population and can ultimately extract greater profits from their labor.
policies.name: Sepúlveda

desc: We have adopted colonial policies in alignment with Las Casas's reasoning that native peoples are not barbarians, and have free will. They should therefore convert to Christianity out of their own free will and cannot be enslaved without consequences.
policies.name: Las Casas

desc: We have adopted colonial policies that stipulate officials who represent our empire will only earn a token salary — in exchange for a generous portion of our colonial profits.
policies.name: Portuguese Captaincies

desc: Our colonies will be governed by one central office, which all regional captaincies will report to. This secures our centralized control over our colonies.
policies.name: Portuguese Governorate General

desc: This establishes the policy that our country will follow for colonial affairs.
entities.name: Colonial Policy

desc: We are not allowed to participate in the parliament and our overlord has significant influence over our economy.
policies.name: No Representation

desc: We have been granted a voice within the parliamentary decisions of our land and restricted the influences of our overlord.
policies.name: Representation in Parliament

desc: Our own influence on the land we govern is detetmined by the whims of our overlord.
entities.name: Colonial Representation

desc: No specific rules will be enforced at court.
policies.name: No Court Etiquette

desc: Basic rules will be enforced at court.
policies.name: Basic Court Etiquette

desc: Rules inspired by the Chinese court will be enforced at ours.
policies.name: Sinicized Court Etiquette

desc: This law establishes which court etiquette rules will be applied.
entities.name: Court Etiquette Law

desc: The state is best served through fully realizing the will of its ruler. Through absolute rule, we can ensure our every pronouncement is carried out without delay — surely, to the greater benefit of all.
policies.name: Absolute Rule

desc: The balance of power between the [
] and the Crown is a delicate matter. Our best option is to keep this balance intact by neither promoting the rights of the ruler, nor curtailing their power.
policies.name: Equal Power Relation

desc: The ruler represents the state, but holds little actual power. All government actions and decisions go through multiple apparatuses of the government rather than being approved by a single ruler.
policies.name: Figurehead Position

desc: The position of the Crown is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Crown

desc: Martial values have always been important in our society, but as we expand our borders, the need for militarization becomes ever more apparent. We must continue this trend, and build a strong nation with military might at its core.
policies.name: Martial Society

desc: A strong nation requires more than military might — it needs a dynamic civil society where artisans, traders, clerics, and institutions of all kinds can flourish, creating prosperous communities that generate wealth, maintain social order, and contribute to the development of a sophisticated state.
policies.name: Civil Society

desc: Our maritime traditions form the very fabric of our society. United in the thrill of taming the sea and venturing into foreign ports, our people have built a name for themselves as masters of naval affairs.
policies.name: Maritime Society

desc: The virtues of Pietism — diligence, sincerity, and a sense of duty above all — are the core values of our society.
policies.name: Prussian Virtues

desc: Our society originated with the ancient Sarmatians. However, Sarmatism is not just a theory of origin, but a cultural and political phenomenon that promotes the ideals of Aristocracy and the Golden Liberty.
policies.name: Sarmatism

desc: Ancient tradition is the foundation of many cultures and civilizations. While progress is what will drive us to greatness, our traditions will always serve us as the reminder of our origins, and as a source for the strength and unity of our people.
entities.name: Cultural Traditions

desc: A system where the taxation is measured by the size of the land, as well as its value. The people have to pay either using silver or crops, and if their land was left uncultivated for a long time, then it is exempt from taxation until it has regained its productivity.
policies.name: Zabiti System

desc: Favored by the majority of the common people as it collects the state share through produce rather than paying the estimate of the crops.
policies.name: Ghalla Bakshi System

desc: The most arbitrary of the three methods, this system finds the average demand of the land of the past decades, and it is taxed according to these demands.
policies.name: Nasaq System

desc: Instead of allowing local taxation laws to develop for the common people within India, organizing them all within the Dahsala Taxation will allow us to properly tax them.
entities.name: Dahsala Taxation

desc: Power is traditionally distributed among the ruling sovereign and the leading elites of our society. It does not challenge the status, and is favorable to neither the head of the state nor to the aristocracy.
policies.name: Traditional Distribution

desc: The balance of power should favor the head of state, as they alone can be trusted to have the best interests of the nation at heart.
policies.name: Favor the Ruler

desc: The Nobility form the backbone of our society, and we could not do without their leadership. We would do well to cultivate their influence.
policies.name: Favor the Elites

desc: The guilds and Burghers are the lifeblood of our people! And, of course, our treasury. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Market Language

policies.name: Favor the Wealthy

desc: Our faith has held our society together in the face of adversity time and time again, thanks to the guidance of our wise Clergy. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language

policies.name: Favor the Clergy

desc: The Catholic Church is the cornerstone of our realm. By elevating our Clergy in matters of governance, we strengthen our ties with Rome and open the coffers of the faithful. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language

policies.name: Favor the Church

desc: The Commoners are the ones who toil daily to provide the basic resources, such as food, that everyone needs regardless of their social status. They, perhaps more than anyone, wish to raise our domain to new heights of prosperity and greatness. We would do well to cultivate their influence.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Common Language

policies.name: Favor the Common People

desc: The Gbara is the deliberative assembly of Mali and is defined in the Malian constitution, the Kouroukan Fouga. The Nobility represent the many clans in our state, and check the power of the ruling Mali.
policies.name: Gbara

desc: Parliament is the de facto successor of the ''Magnum Concilium'', and a major pillar of the English government. Parliament's primary function is to check the power of the England by requiring mandatory consultation on taxation and legislation, preventing absolute rule.
policies.name: English Parliament

desc: The Nobility, the Clergy, and the Burghers have formed a deliberative assembly called the ''Cortes de Navarra'', which has the duty to approve laws and taxes, and to investigate legal transgressions. While all Estates debate together, each of them votes as a separate assembly. The position of each Estate is previously decided internally by the majority. In order to achieve a resolution to any issue they deliberate, all Three Estates must agree on the action. Their power allows them to dethrone and elect rulers when needed, and overall to keep the power of the monarch in check.
policies.name: Cortes de Navarra

desc: The Governing Senate is the highest governmental body of the Russian State, and has been created as a replacement of the Boyar Duma. Combining the roles of the legislative, judicial, and executive powers, the Senate is a powerful institution which is subordinate to none but the rulers themselves.
policies.name: Governing Senate

desc: The State Council is the supreme state advisory body of Russia, created to act as a mediating party between the autocratic regime and the regional Dumas introduced by the Speransky Liberalization Reform reform. The State Council examines proposed laws and oversees the budget and state expenditures, although it lacks the authority to propose changes. Instead, it makes recommendations based on the current situation.
policies.name: State Council

desc: The Estates General is the assembly of the feudal government of French. It has a legislative and consultative role, and represents the three estates of the country: the Nobility, the Clergy, and the Commoners, which itself encompasses the Burghers. Unlike other Parliaments and Assemblies, the approval of the Estates General when making adjustments to the law, such as tax increases, is optional.
policies.name: Estates General

desc: Born from the ashes of the Ancien Régime, the Assemblée Nationale is the conversion of the old Estates General into a modern parliament. The Nobility and Clergy are no longer the dominant powers of the assembly, while the Burghers and the Commoners take a more active role in the events of the State.
policies.name: Assemblée Nationale

desc: The ''Cortes de Castilla'' represent the estates and several cities with voting rights in the Crown of Castile.
policies.name: Cortes de Castilla

desc: The Cortes, our Parliament, has been empowered as the primary political force in our country thanks to the efforts and fight of the Comuneros.
policies.name: Empowered Cortes

desc: As a result of the Revolt of the ''Comuneros'', Crown will now have a stronger grip on the ''Cortes de Castilla''.
policies.name: Reinforced Cortes de Castilla

desc: The Hanseatic Kontor is the basis of our financial success. The many offices we hold across Europe serve as diplomatic ties between us and the host countries, as well as providing seats of power for our local Burghers.
policies.name: Favor the Kontors

desc: One of the most influential cornerstones of our administration, the title of ''Eristavi'' is granted to powerful noble families, allowing them the undisputed authority to recruit and lead armies under their banner. Those who hold this office also enjoy a dominant position in our internal affairs.

mods.label: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier

policies.name: Office of the Eristavi

desc: The Reformed House Rules are a system of joint governance for the Austrian lands, granting all male family members equal status while reserving special privileges for the eldest.
policies.name: Reformed House Rules

desc: Distribution of Power determines how authority is divided among the ruler, administrative bodies, and estates. The state is a complex and fragile entity — a well-balanced power distribution ensures stability, while giving any single institution too much power risks breeding tyranny or administrative paralysis.
entities.name: Distribution of Power

desc: It is our sacred duty to look after the holy sites under our control, and to protect any pilgrims within our lands.
policies.name: Safeguard Holy Sites

desc: In the mission to spread the true faith, we must never waver in our conviction, and be ready to root out heresy wherever it springs up — by force, if need be.
policies.name: Combat Heresy

desc: As our state grows, we inevitably become exposed to wrongful teachings. We must not tolerate heathens or heretics within our city walls! Therefore, we shall allow these nonbelievers to dwell in our cities only if they convert to the true faith.
policies.name: Expulsion of Heathens

desc: Our cause is not the defense of our religion, nor the forceful expansion of our faith. Instead, we focus on the very nature of being, exploring the relationship between the mortal and the divine realms.
policies.name: Pursuit of Knowledge

desc: While monarchies and republics may be content to simply exist in the world, a Holy State requires a deeper, more spiritual calling. This Divine Cause shall guide our hand towards a glorious destiny.
entities.name: Divine Cause

desc: Both Sunday and Saturday are considered sacred.
policies.name: Allow Double Sabbath

desc: The observance of the Sabbath is no longer necessary when celebrating the Lord's Day on Sunday.
policies.name: Forbid Double Sabbath

desc: The Sabbath has been the holy day reserved to God since the times of Moses. It may still be preserved as a day of rest, or it could be considered to be superseded by the Lord's Day on Sunday.
entities.name: Double Sabbath

desc: Settlements are encouraged to trade crops between them.
policies.name: Shared Crops

desc: Settlements are meant to be self-sustaining.
policies.name: Decentralized Farming Villages

desc: Distribution of crops between settlements will be carried out at the highest level.
policies.name: Resource Extraction Bureaus

desc: This law defines the distribution of all crops grown in our settlements.
entities.name: Economic Law

desc: This proviso limits property appropriation by requiring that when someone claims unowned resources, there must equally valuable resources available for others. The government moderates this balance and ensures that private property acquisition does not deprive others of their equal opportunity to gain wealth.
policies.name: Lockean Proviso

desc: The economic security of the state is based on our ability to wage and win wars. Manufactories in our state should have no other purpose than fueling our military ambitions.
policies.name: War Economy

desc: Economics play a vital role within the apparatus of the state. The complex systems of trade, finance, and luxury must be handled by our intellectuals and scholars to best serve the needs of the government.
policies.name: Embrace the Economic Theory

desc: Merchants from all over the world should be able to trade within our borders. Abandoning the narrowness of mercantilism, the state will now gain easier access to foreign goods — and ducats.
policies.name: Free Trade

desc: Royal charters are allowances granted by the Crown to individuals or trade companies that bestow them with unique rights and powers. These charters are an excellent way for us to support ventures — and exploit opportunities — abroad.
policies.name: Royal Charters

desc: To strengthen our economic position and attract immigrants, we will rely on a bureaucratic system, designed to administrate our efforts in great detail. These chambers will organize everything from the construction of new manufactories to the distribution of new settlers arriving in our territory.
policies.name: Cameralism

desc: The pirates that run amok in the republic cannot be trusted to bathe themselves, let alone to govern a nation whose future hands on the edge of a cutlass. A Consortium formed of the most influential black market merchants shall be established as its true governors. Profit must come before liberty.
policies.name: Black Market Consortium

desc: A nation's economic policy sets out specific economic objectives and means to achieve them, and makes decisions and creates regulations for taxation, spending, currency, trade, and more.
entities.name: Economic Policy

desc: Education must be freely accessible to all those who seek it. We shall permit unrestrained access to the wisdom held within our institutions of learning, and throw the doors open wide to receive our people, that they may more readily develop the innovation and intellectual sophistication that will set us apart from other states.
policies.name: Open Institutions

desc: A balanced approach may be best if we are to keep our heads of faith and general populace satisfied while also providing valuable knowledge and access to education. Let us find a reasonable middle ground between the theological and secular schools of thought.
policies.name: Mixed Institutions

desc: The national identity of our people is inextricably tied to our faith and the headship of our clerical leaders. In order to better solidify the role of religion in our state, we should align our educational institutions with our religious ones, and instruct our people accordingly.
policies.name: Theological Institutions

desc: Heathens and heresy are the factors that most strenuously test our beliefs. They seduce otherwise pious people away from the true faith with poisonous thoughts, drawing them away from the light to be devoured by darkness. Our missionaries must be learned and have unshakeable belief if they are to counter this corrosive evil.
policies.name: Education of the Missionaries

desc: The fate of our nation twists in the hands of the divine, who hold dominion over all mundane matters. But it is the sacred duty of our ruler to interpret signs from the heavens, and communicate them to our people, so that we remain always favored above all other nations. To avoid any dangerous misinterpretations, the state must focus its efforts on thoroughly educating future rulers.
policies.name: Education of the Theocrat

desc: Our ruler might represent the will of our government, but all humans are prone to human error. With the support of a highly educated court behind them, our ruler is less likely to commit a grave mistake in judgment.
policies.name: Education of the Court

desc: Knowledge and education are two of the most enriching aspects in anyone's life, and therefore, the state must ensure our people have access to both. We are all born with free will and free thought, and it is the state's duty to preserve these natural rights, which are held by all our people.
policies.name: Education of the People

desc: Private institutions combining the functions of a school with those of a religious shrine, these academies educate elite students in classical texts and Confucian philosophy while preparing them for civil service examinations. While officially an apparatus of the state, these institutions are given extensive authority and special privileges that set them apart from other government entities.
policies.name: Confucian Academies

desc: It is mandatory for our Nobility to undergo thorough schooling. With the goal of improving our government functions, every member of the elite classes shall be rigorously educated in the study of law, art, and Latin.
policies.name: Compulsory Education for Nobility

desc: The education of our elites is of vital importance. By providing our upper-class citizens with ample access to appropriate works of art, we will further our cultural goals, both at home and abroad, through the creation of legendary works and the amplification of our splendor!
entities.name: Education of the Elites

desc: What use are reading and writing to those whose sole purpose is to tend crops? The masses are best left to their fields and flocks, innocent of the many dangerous ideas hidden between book covers.
policies.name: Uneducated Masses

desc: The millennia-old, tried-and-true method of letting our religious institutions take responsibility for educating our people, while the state focuses on more important tasks.
policies.name: Religious Teachings

desc: A pious education, focusing on ensuring that students are well-versed in the workings of the divine. Theology can be more useful than mathematics, after all... albeit perhaps not in every situation.
policies.name: Devout Education

desc: The sacred process by which a skilled mentor passes down a lifetime of knowledge to a protégé. While many of these mentorship-apprentice arrangements are formally arranged, eager learners can also be taught by their families, established elder members of society, or even their guild quartermasters.
policies.name: Individual Apprenticeships

desc: Wisdom is passed down to younger generations through methods such as storytelling or the performing arts. Venerable members of a community tell and re-tell ancient tales and the lessons learned from them, which young listeners will memorize and repeat in the future. In this way, the history of our people will be preserved from generation to generation by those who lived it.
policies.name: Oral Tradition

desc: Our Church will be responsible for educating the people of our nation. These efforts will be financially supported through tax revenue collected from upon the landowning elite.
policies.name: Presbyterian Education

desc: Why centralize education in formal institutions when the printing-press has allowed every household to become its own school? We will let our people educate themselves, giving them the responsibility of deciding what knowledge they find worthy of acquiring.
policies.name: Personal Religious Education

desc: Young people learn best when the knowledge is presented in the form of gripping, memorable tales, and they are both captivating and easy to understand. Much can be learned from the fantastic stories of our ancestors, and we shall make sure our people understand these lessons well.
policies.name: Epic Tradition

desc: Young people learn best when the knowledge is presented in the form of gripping, memorable tales, and they are both captivating and easy to understand. Much can be learned from the fantastic stories of our ancestors, and we shall make sure our people understand these lessons well.
policies.name: Epic Tradition

desc: Houses of worship are the home of the divine, not the classroom. Let us keep secular and religious instruction separate, as the mundane and divine realms are.
policies.name: Secular Education

desc: An education method that teaches the masses about Hinduism without seperating anyone into castes.
policies.name: Vedic Education

desc: The education of our population is of vital importance. By providing our people with ample access to the appropriate materials, regardless of their place in the social hierarchy, we will create a more educated and artistically fluent population, and further our governmental goals both at home and abroad.
entities.name: Education of the Masses

desc: The Prince-Elector are at their peak of their power as they expand their ranks by three additional seats, and also add three additional Archbishop-Elector. Additionally, they gain the right to elect an Anti-King who can replace the current Hre in the Imperial Diet if left unchallenged. This gives the Electors the de facto power to force a re-election of the current Hre.
policies.name: Elector Council

desc: The Prince-Elector expand their ranks by two additional seats, and also add two additional Archbishop-Elector. Only significant promises and pledges can earn the favor of an Prince-Elector.
policies.name: Expanded Electors

desc: The Prince-Elector expand their ranks by one additional Prince-Elector and one additional Archbishop-Elector. Additionally, earning an Prince-Elector's vote is reliant than ever on pledges and promises.
policies.name: Electorate

desc: The number of Prince-Elector is limited to seven. Votes for Emperorship can be favored, though pledges and promises are a powerful and reliable tool to win an Prince-Elector's vote.
policies.name: Limited Electors

desc: The Prince-Elector are curtailed, and one of their voting rights is transferred to the Hre.
policies.name: Integrated Electors

desc: The Prince-Elector are a group of powerful Nobility and Clergy who have the privilege to vote for their next Hre.
entities.name: Electorate Organization

desc: Prince-Elector are free to adhere to whichever denominations of our state religion they prefer. This does not, however, condone heathenry, which will not be tolerated.
policies.name: Only Imperial Religion Group

desc: Prince-Elector are required to follow the Imperial religion in order to maintain their status.
policies.name: Only Imperial Religion

desc: Religion is a major pillar of the Holy Roman Empire for Emperors and Prince-Elector alike.
entities.name: Electorate Religious Law

desc: By permitting enclosures, we allow communal lands used by local populations to be privately owned, and for exclusive use by the owner.
policies.name: Enclosure Allowed

desc: Communal lands are protected from becoming Enclosures and cannot be privately owned.
policies.name: Enclosure Disallowed

desc: Communal lands are further enclosed or privatized in order to support the rise of commercial agriculture and the growth of industrialization.
policies.name: Enclosure Act

desc: The Enclosure Movement is the process by which formerly communal land is surrounded by walls or fences, and thus transformed into private property.
entities.name: Enclosure Movement

desc: As the noblest and bravest denizens of the realm, the Knights Companion are the very embodiment of courage, loyalty, and camaraderie. By elevating the most loyal members of the peerage, the Crown ensures that this prestigious order remains a bastion of chivalry, each member valiantly serving both the monarch and the nation.
policies.name: Knights Companion

desc: Through the inclusion of distinguished foreign rulers, diplomats, and knights, the Stranger Knights bring a wealth of diverse perspectives, and help the Crown extend its reach over our lands.
policies.name: Stranger Knights

desc: With divine guidance and unwavering faith, the Holy Brotherhood of the Order of the Garter is composed of esteemed bishops and other senior clerics. By elevating these devout servants of faith, the Crown will strengthen the spiritual foundation of the realm.
policies.name: Holy Brotherhood

desc: Recognizing the power of culture and the arts to inspire and elevate the human spirit, the Crown uses the Order of the Garter as a means to foster creativity and promote the talents of the realm's most gifted citizens.
policies.name: Patron of Arts

desc: In an act of compassion and benevolence, the Order extends its charity to men-at-arms who return home from service impoverished, and knights who are left disinherited and landless by war.
policies.name: Alms Knights

desc:
The Order of the Garter is a prestigious symbol of our realm's highest ideals, transcending time and uniting worthy people of diverse backgrounds and talents.

Whether composed of the monarch's favorites, esteemed foreign dignitaries, devout members of the clergy, gifted artisans, or valiant warriors, this venerable order is the pinnacle of nobility and virtue.
entities.name: Order of the Garter

desc: Tax is directly sourced from the [
], with a progressive rate structure that taxes [
policies.name: Income Taxation

desc: The bulk of tax revenue primarily comes from customs duties and excise taxes, which are shouldered by the Burghers.
policies.name: Trade Taxation

desc: ], with privileges dictating the level of taxation. Business as usual.
policies.name: Traditional Taxation

desc: Stable revenue is key for a functioning government. By implementing a legal taxation framework, we can regulate tax collection from individuals and entities.
entities.name: Taxation

desc: Our patriarchate will integrate this aspect into its core beliefs, embraced by all our members.
policies.name: Accept the Tenet of Essence

desc: Our patriarchate will reject this aspect into its core beliefs, embraced by all our members.
policies.name: Reject the Tenet of Essence

desc: Known also as ousia (''ουσία''), this tenet represents the interpretation of the Divinity of God as being the same as the Divinity of Christ.
entities.name: Essence

desc: A maximum 12-hour workday is enforced, and regular inspections of factories are carried out.
policies.name: Decent Conditions

desc: In addition to regulated working hours and factory inspections, additional protection is offered for child workers, limiting their work hours and mandating educational opportunities.
policies.name: Fair Conditions

desc: Factory owners are free to run their businesses as they please. Accidents are a frequent issue, workers often experience exploitation, and workplace fatalities are all too common.
policies.name: Unregulated Conditions

desc: The expansion of our manufacturing industry is accelerating industrialization and boosting production capacity. As factory workers become increasingly central to the economy, regulating their rights in order to prevent exploitation becomes vital.
entities.name: Factory Working Conditions

desc: Customary laws are commonly known and practiced in our country. Famous compilations of medieval customs include ''De Legibus et Consuetudinibus Angliae'' for England, ''Sachsenspiegel'' for northern Germany, or the ''Usatges of Barcelona'' for Catalonia.
policies.name: By Tradition

desc: The laws of our country reflect the nature of our people and the sovereign authority of our ruler, as expressed in the famous formula ''rex in regno suo est imperator regni sui'' - 'The king is emperor in his own kingdom.'
policies.name: By Blood

desc: These are the laws that organize the feudal society of our country.
entities.name: Feudal 'De Jure' Laws

desc: Culture is similar in many ways to religion, in that it dictates social values and traditions and is influenced by the environment in which it develops. Accepting foreigners in our population for who they are, and allowing them to live their lifestyles undisturbed, will ensure a peaceful coexistence.
policies.name: Allow Foreign Rituals

desc: Although foreign ideas can be alien to us, we should nevertheless stay abreast of interesting ideas and innovations in these foreign cultures, and adopt those that would serve us and our people. This will ease assimilation of foreigners into our society while increasing our own cultural influence.
policies.name: Integrate Foreign Traditions

desc: The cultural aspects of our minority population are of little concern to us. As long as they provide soldiers for our military efforts when required, these foreigners are free to practice their traditions.
policies.name: Blood Tax of Foreigners

desc: This legal framework seeks to maximize the economic exploitation and governance of territories we have conquered. The subjugated population is legally obliged to undergo reorganization, resulting in the establishment of rural settlements. This system is aimed at integrating the locals into our administration, converting them at a steady pace and expanding our influence.
policies.name: Agrarian Constitution

desc: Despite our aptitude towards culture and preserving our ways, there is much benefit for us should we choose to study the ways of our Chinese neighbors.
policies.name: Promote Chinese Traditions

desc: As we strive to preserve and weave our traditions into the annals of history, we must stay vigilant lest we become just another satellite state to a greater power.
policies.name: Limit Chinese Traditions

desc: As our state grows in size, so does the complexity of our social structures. Cultural unity within our state is no longer a given, and we now require policies to establish and maintain internal peace.
entities.name: Foreign Cultural Law

desc: The Chinese system of writing will be used.
policies.name: Sinicized Writing

desc: This law declares which script or writing system must be used to write official documentation.
entities.name: Formal Script Law

desc: The Five Percent Tax is collected from all people, regardless of their status.
policies.name: For All Estates

desc: The Five Percent Tax is collected only from the Commoners.
policies.name: Only for Peasants

desc: A new tax proposed by the Minister of Finance, accounting for one-twentieth of the annual income.
entities.name: Machault's Five Percent Tax

desc: The state will collect a Hearth tax to assist in covering the growing expenses of the treasury. Levying the tax however will greatly anger members of the peasantry.
policies.name: Levying Fouage Tax

desc: The levying of the Fouage Hearth tax has been rescinded, making the peasantry less dissatisfied with the state.
policies.name: Rescinded Levying of the Fouage Tax

policy_names: Rescinded Levying of the Fouage Tax

desc: A large Hearth Tax levied against the peasantry in order to assist in covering the growing expenses of the treasury.
entities.name: Fouage Tax Levy

desc: The legality of Jansenism currently exists in a state of limbo, with the ''Unigenitus'' decree unimplemented. Followers of Jansenism are treated equally to other religious sects.
policies.name: No Formal Law

desc: The Unigenitus Decree has been codified into law, outlawing any form of practice of Jansenism. Known followers of Jansenism are forced to pay the ''Cinquantième'' tax.
policies.name: Unigenitus Decree

desc: A doctrine following the teachings of Saint Augustine, ''Jansenism'' emphasizes predestination, the profound and lasting effects of original sin, and rigorous morality. It has increasingly come under threat with the rise of Absolutism in France, as well as having been officially condemned by the Roman Bull ''Unigenitus''.
entities.name: Status of Jansenism

desc: Special privileges have been given to the Lutheranism population throughout France, preventing their persecution. However, the France's policy is seen as heresy by the Catholicism Clergy.
policies.name: Edict of Lutheranism Tolerance

desc: Special privileges have been given to the population throughout France who follow these new, reformed faiths, preventing their persecution.
policies.name: Edict of Religious Tolerance

desc: The Edict of Nantes grants considerable rights to the religious minorities throughout France, putting them on an equal footing with followers of the Catholicism faith. It also ends the decades-long persecution of our Huguenot citizens.
policies.name: Edict of Nantes

desc: The court has deemed the rise of Protestantism a serious threat to the stability of France, and practice of the heretic faith is now considered high treason.
policies.name: Edict of Fontainebleau

desc: The continued rise of Protestantism and other Reformation faiths has led the council to expand the previous Edict of Fontainebleau to target all heretical faiths.
policies.name: Expanded Edict of Fontainebleau

desc: The rise of Protestantism in France has reached a crucial point, forcing the court to take extreme action. Under the Edict of Châteaubriant, followers of heretical beliefs are prevented from holding public offices, and conducting trade throughout France.
policies.name: Edict of Châteaubriant

desc: The Reformation is sweeping across Europe, and France is on the front lines of its outbreak. State policy towards these emerging zealots will be critical in making them our friends — or foes.
entities.name: Reformation Edicts

desc: Establishes the ''taille'' as an ordinary tax, expanding the state's potential revenue collection.
policies.name: Permanent Tax

desc: Establish the ''taille'' as an exceptional tax, which can only be collected in times of need.
policies.name: Exceptional Only

desc: The ''taille'' is a tax imposed on each household based on the amount of land it occupies. The Clergy and Nobility are exempt.
entities.name: Taille

desc: The Free Imperial Cities are no more. No town or city will be under the protection of the Hre.
policies.name: Free Cities Abolished

desc: Free Cities no longer enjoy the protection of the Hre when defending themselves from ambitious princes.
policies.name: Unprotected Free Cities

desc: Free Cities are protected by the Hre and enjoy extensive autonomy over facilitating trade in their markets.
policies.name: Free Cities

desc: Free Cities autonomy is limited by the Hre. Though still capable of performing diplomacy of their own, the cities are now one step closer to becoming part of the administration of the Hre.
policies.name: Cities of the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetLeaderTitle]

desc: Free Cities are now under the direct administration of the Hre. With heavily limited autonomy, the city-states are de facto outposts within the Holy Roman Empire for the Imperial Crown.
policies.name: Direct Imperial Cities

desc: The Free Cities of the Holy Roman Empire are self-ruling cities with autonomy. They are usually where Imperial Diet meetings are held.
entities.name: Free Cities

desc: The Holy Roman Empire is first and foremost German, and the privilege of a Free Imperial City reflects this reality.
policies.name: Only Germanic Free Cities

desc: The Empire has a long history with the Netherlandish, Swiss, and Italian. This justifies allowing non-German states to receive the desired Free Imperial City status.
policies.name: Brethren-Cultured Free Cities

desc: The status of a Free Imperial City is no longer tied to geography or culture. Every nation who wishes to may petition the Hre for this title.
policies.name: Indiscriminate Free City Rights

desc: Obtaining the status of a Free Imperial City is not easy. This exclusive title must be conferred by the Hre.
entities.name: Free City Rights

desc: While previous attempts have been made to establish colonies in the New World, they proved ineffective. However, with renewed financial backing from the state, establishing settlements in the New World should now be less challenging and more rewarding.
policies.name: New World Settlements

desc: The Indian spice trade, while contested by other European powers, still remains a valuable market in which to establish a base of power.
policies.name: Ambitions in the Far East

desc: Having grown more established in India and the Far East, the French East India Company has been opened to expand the current French influence in the region. Only time will tell if the company will prove profitable, however...
policies.name: French East India Company

desc: Having overcome decades of turmoil, France has reached a point where it can finance overseas exploration. New policies will enable the court to pursue colonial ambitions with greater efficiency
entities.name: Colonial Aspirations

desc: The Golden Bull is the decree of the Holy Roman Empire which defines and creates the constitutional structure of the Empire, especially the Electoral College. Other laws and Imperial Reforms all build on the Golden Bull.

mods.label: Enable Leave the Holy Roman Empire Peace
Forbidden Unjustified Wars Against Other Members

policies.name: Seal the Golden Bull

desc: Without the Golden Bull, the Holy Roman Empire's electoral and constitutional arrangements remain a patchwork of custom, precedent, and shifting alliances. The absence of a formal decree leaves the [Electoral College] more susceptible to disputes, intrigue, and political maneuvering.
policies.name: Uncodified Electoral Order

desc: The Golden Bull is the decree of the Holy Roman Empire which defines and creates the constitutional structure of the Empire, especially the Electoral College. Other laws and Imperial Reforms all build on the Golden Bull.
entities.name: Golden Bull

desc: ''Arti Minori'' refers to the smaller trade associations that represent artisan crafters and other occupations of lesser scale and importance. These guilds focus on specialized skills such as saddlemaking, locksmithing, or carpentry, and they hold the lowest status within the merchant sphere.

mods.label: Maximum RGO Size in Towns & Cities

policies.name: Arti Minori

desc: ''Arti Mediane'' serve as intermediate guilds occupying a middle position between the ''Arti Minori'' and ''Arti Maggiori''. These guilds represent trades and professions of moderate scale and influence, such as blacksmithing and shoemaking, and acted as a bridge between the smaller specialized crafts and the more dominant industries.

mods.label: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Arti Mediane

desc: The ''Arti Maggiori'' are the largest and most influential merchant guilds. These guilds represent the major industries and trades that hold significant economic and political power, such as the textile industry or the banking and finance sector.
