policies.name: Arti Maggiori

desc: The powerful mercantile institutes that make up our social fabric, the merchant guilds are an important proponent of our continued prosperity and affluence. Though all of them are important, it is undeniable that some are better at obtaining power and influence than others.
entities.name: Primacy of Florentine Guilds

desc: Meaning the 'tenth part', it is a system of revenue collection which establishes that a tenth of one's income should be donated in the name of the Gurū.
policies.name: Dasvandh Tax

desc: Meaning 'act towards happiness', it is the wedding ceremony for Sikhism as defined by Guru Amar Das. The hymns sung in it celebrate the union with the divine.
policies.name: Ānada Kāraja

desc: Men an women are equal under Ik Onkar, and thus both are equally valid to be part of the Sangat monastic community, and even to lead it.
policies.name: Sangat Equality

desc: The teachings established by Guru Amar Das.
entities.name: guru_amar_das Teachings

desc: A script developed and standardized by guru_angad, it will become the primary scripture for Sikhism.
policies.name: Gurmukhī Script

desc: A communal kitchen attached to any temple, they will serve food freely to all people, regardless of their creed, status, or ethnicity.
policies.name: Langar Community

desc: Wrestling arenas for the people to practice will serve not only as a way to keep their bodies healthy, but also as an improvement of their martial prowess.
policies.name: Mall Akhāṛā

desc: A collection of hymns from past Gurū compiled by guru_arjan that will serve as the basis for our holy scriptures.
policies.name: Adi Granth

desc: By enshrining the sacred scriptures inside the holy temples, we will turn them as the place of residence of Ik Onkar and a focus of pilgrimage for all Sikhism faithful.
policies.name: Holy Abode

desc: Our belief in Sikhism is strong, and we will not abandon it even under the threat of torture or even death.
policies.name: Martyrdom

desc: While the Khalsa is intended to be the protector of Sikhism, not all the faithful are part of it. As such, it inherently proves there is pluralism inside the faith, and that is something that enriches us.
policies.name: Sikhism Pluralism

desc: A 'war of righteousness' is any war that serves the purpose of defending Sikhism and its followers. War should be a last resort, but all must be ready to wage it to defend the faith and stop tyranny.
policies.name: Dharamyudh

desc: A collection of various texts of poetry composed by Guru Gobind Singh, it is considered equal in status to the Adi Granth and it is enshrined next to it in the temples.
policies.name: Dasam Granth

desc: The teachings established by Guru Gobind Singh.
entities.name: guru_gobind_singh Teachings

desc: The Guru Granth Sahib is the final and sovereign eternal Gurū, which shall be the guiding light for all followers of Sikhism.
policies.name: Eternally Living Gurū

desc: The teachings encoded in the Guru Granth Sahib guide our society to live in peace and harmony, based on Ik Onkar and His justice.
policies.name: Divine Justice

desc: The Guru Granth Sahib was composed during the course of many years and by more than one Gurū, but it has now reached its definite and eternal form. Its writings shall no longer be altered in any way.
policies.name: Unchanging Writing

desc: The teachings established in the Guru Granth Sahib.
entities.name: Guru Granth Sahib Teachings

desc: Diseases and pestilence are the bane of humanity. We shall treat all sick people diligently, so that we can ensure a healthy society.
policies.name: Treat the Sick

desc: The spiritual powers of the Gurū are undeniable, as they have been said to have known truths and facts that they had no way of knowing through normal methods. At the same time, people apparently illiterate may be able to discuss theology with the most learned scholar.
policies.name: Unexpected Knowledge

desc: No matter how much one has learned, there are always sources of knowledge outside of one's grasp, and people who have mastered them. Even the younger ones may harbor knowledge out of the understanding of the more senior minds. In this sense, all minds are like that of an infant.
policies.name: Young Humility

desc: The teachings established by Guru Har Krishan.
entities.name: guru_har_krishan Teachings

desc: The ones at the head of our many religious administrations should not show partiality towards any opinion, but serve dutifully the interests of Sikhism.
policies.name: Impartial Manji Heads

desc: If one plucks a flower with one hand and gives it away with the other, both hands get the same fragrance. As such, no matter our different religious beliefs, we are all touched by the same divine spirit.
policies.name: Fragrance of a Flower

desc: Our natural environment is not there to serve us, but for us to live in harmony with it. As such, we must protect it and provide for it as much as it provides for us.
policies.name: Nature Guardian

desc: The teachings established by Guru Har Rai.
entities.name: guru_har_rai Teachings

desc: The 'Throne of the Timeless One' will serve as the unquestionable seat of power for our Gurū and Sikhism.
policies.name: Akal Takht

desc: The power of military should not be used to oppress and become a tyrant, but to protect the vulnerable from such tyrants.
policies.name: Protection of the Poor

desc: Only by combining temporal power and spiritual authority under the figure of the Gurū can Sikhism truly achieve its deserved glory.
policies.name: Mīrī Pīrī

desc: Meaning 'share and consume', it is one of the pillars of guru_nanak. It encourages the sharing of all that is available and the collective consume of it by the community.
policies.name: Vaṇḍ Chakō

desc: Meaning 'work honestly', it is one of the pillars of guru_nanak. It means dedication and honestly to hard labor, as exercise of what Ik Onkar has given us.
policies.name: Kirat Karō

desc: Meaning 'recite His name', it is one of the pillars of guru_nanak. It means to meditate and contemplate the many names of Ik Onkar, to achieve connection with Him.
policies.name: Nām Japō

desc: Through serious dedication and communal voluntary work, the holiest and most splendorous of Sikhism cities can be built.
policies.name: Urbanization Projects

desc: The scripture is the holiest of books, and it has to be embellished by the appropriate hymns lauding its glory.
policies.name: Scripture Hymns

desc: A system of missionaries and preachers, they will spread the Sikhism further away from the Gurū while serving as tax collectors at the same time.
policies.name: Masand System

desc: The teachings established by Guru Ram Das.
entities.name: guru_ram_das Teachings

desc: The solemn vow of a follower of Sikhism is to be understood as been made in the presence of Ik Onkar, and as such it should be unbreakable.
policies.name: Word of a Sikhism

desc: If a Gurū stays only in one place, the message of Sikhism will not be able to spread. A Gurū must thus travel and have contact with foreign peoples and beliefs.
policies.name: Gurū Travels

desc: Enemies of the true faith will always persecute the faithful, but our beliefs are strong and they will not be able to break us.
policies.name: Resist Persecution

desc: The teachings established by Guru Tegh Bahadur.
entities.name: guru_tegh_bahadur Teachings

desc: Our military frontier is fully maintained and ready to protect the country from incoming threats.
policies.name: Frontier Maintained

desc: Due to the lack of funding, our military frontier is currently not maintained and thus vulnerable in case of enemy incursions.
policies.name: Frontier Not Maintained

desc: We have established a military frontier to protect the nation from heathen hordes that are encroaching upon our borders.
entities.name: Military Frontier

desc: The harem is scattered over several locations, and the concubines as itinerant as the royal court. When a concubine has given birth to a son, she is sent with him to a provincial location to oversee his education and train him for future governorship.
policies.name: Dispersed Harem

desc: Our harem is not for the eyes of the masses outside the royal court. As such, it holds a more secluded role within the household, and is strictly forbidden to directly interfere in the affairs of the monarch.
policies.name: Secluded Harem

desc: Our harem does not only provide legitimate heirs, but is also a symbol of the royal family's wealth, power, and prestige. The beauty and talents of the harem's members are therefore proudly displayed to the public eye.
policies.name: Public Harem

desc: The monarch is a mere puppet, dancing at the fingertips of cunning concubines and eunuchs. The true power of the state lies in the hands of the harem, and state affairs are handled by the women of the royal court.
policies.name: Powerful Harem

desc: The harem is a glittering, ostentatious display of wealth, and focused primarily on the ruler's personal pleasure. The concubines must be the most exquisite lineages, and they spend their days lounging in the pinnacle of luxury.
policies.name: Extravagant Harem

desc: The harem is a significant institution within the royal household, and secures the production of heirs for the succession.
entities.name: Harem Laws

desc: ] is not determined by the laws but by the [Succession Law] itself.
policies.name: Special Succession

desc: ] from the same religion as the prevailing one ensures that the beliefs and practices of the population and Crown are aligned. While this policy can contribute to religious cohesion, it may also limit opportunities for those of different faiths to assume leadership positions.
policies.name: Same Religion

desc: ] from the same religious group is often desirable in order to maintain religious and cultural continuity and prevent potential religious conflicts. This policy can help safeguard the stability of the realm by minimizing religious divisions within the leadership, at the expense of individuals from faiths considered to be 'heathen' being able to assume leadership roles.
policies.name: Same Religious Group

desc: Faith is personal, and does not reflect nor compromise an individual's ability to lead. The [
] may worship any religion and still assume leadership roles. This policy carries a higher risk of religious conflicts within the leadership, while promoting religious freedom and general acceptance.
policies.name: Any Religion

desc: The ability to decide the religion of the [

] holds significant importance in matters of succession and governance. It allows rulers and governments to maintain religious stability, ensuring that the beliefs and practices of the ruler align with those of the majority of their subjects. Ultimately, the power to determine the religion of the heir represents an important element in the fine balance of religious freedom, governance, and societal harmony.
entities.name: Heir Religion

desc: Vaishnavism is the [Hindu Branch] centered around the worship of Viṣṇu and his ten [
policies.name: Vaishnavism

desc: Shaivism is the [Hindu Branch] revering Śiva as the supreme [
]. It is the [Hindu Branch] more focused on asceticism and yoga.
policies.name: Shaivism

desc: Shaktism is the [Hindu Branch] centered around the worship of the Mother Goddess, known as Devī or Śakti, represented and revered in her many different forms.
policies.name: Shaktism

desc: Smartism is the [Hindu Branch] that does not consider any [
] to be above any other, and instead worships equally the five [
] Gaṇeśa, Śiva, Śakti, Viṣṇu, and Sūrya.
policies.name: Smartism

desc: The specific traditions and beliefs followed by this [Hindu Branch].
entities.name: Tradition

desc: We must focus our energy on the holy missions that affect those within our borders: to protect the faithful, aid the less fortunate, and fulfill our spiritual duties.
policies.name: Internal Mission

desc: The spread of our holy faith must be our foremost mission. We cannot rest until we have defeated all enemies of our religion!

mods.label: War Score vs other Religion Efficiency

policies.name: External Mission

desc: The affairs of our theocracy cannot be focused on only one aspect. It is in the best interests of both our state and our religion to invest equally in our internal and external missions.
policies.name: Balanced Mission

desc: Although religion is the driving force of our ambitions, it is undeniable that our state depends on the might of the Ducat. Fortunately, religion and monetization go hand in hand.
policies.name: Commercial Mission

desc: Our faith is at constant risk from heathens and heretics alike. The only ones who we can count on are other followers of our religion - our brothers and sisters in faith. It is our duty to protect them from the forces of evil.
policies.name: Mission of Protection

desc: Our mission is to seek out the misguided, primitive peoples across the world and teach them the proper way to live and believe, so that they too may join us in our divinity.
policies.name: Mission to Civilize

desc: The seas are filled with heathens and villains, plundering the ships of our brethren in faith! At this rate, pilgrims will never be able to safely visit our holy sites if we do not undertake the divine mission to eliminate this piratical menace on the high seas.
policies.name: Mission on the High Seas

desc: The guideline for our every action is the Holy Mission we have been granted from our divine ruler. The vision the higher power has foreseen for us shall come to fruition!
entities.name: Holy Mission

desc: The Crown makes regular financial contributions towards maintain a network of strong fortifications throughout our kingdom.
policies.name: Végvár System

desc: Our great fortresses are currently in disrepair due to Crown being unable to finance their maintenance.
policies.name: Not Maintained

desc: Our domain is surrounded by many aggressive neighbors. To protect our people, we must invest in fortifications on our frontiers, enduring they are adequately funded and supplied.
entities.name: The Frontier Fortresses

desc: The borders of our country are open to anyone, and all may come and go freely.
policies.name: Open Borders

desc: Nobody is permitted to leave or enter our country.
policies.name: Closed Borders

desc: ] is allowed in or out of the country.
entities.name: Border Controls

desc: The Holy Roman Empire has no formal geographic subdivisions.
policies.name: No Imperial Circles

desc: The Holy Roman Empire is divided into Imperial Circles, each governed by a designated [Circle Leader] who coordinates their region's affairs.
policies.name: Imperial Circles Established

desc: The Imperial Circles divides the Holy Roman Empire into geographic administrative regions, each led by a designated [Circle Leader].
entities.name: Imperial Circles

desc: Having never been formally codified, the system of the Court Assembly is in dire need of reform.
policies.name: Traditional Diet

desc:
The earliest form of Imperial Diet represents the traditional order of the Holy Roman Empire. Only the Prince-Elector, Archbishop-Elector, and Imperial Prince may participate, excluding Free Imperial City and lower ecclesiastical entities from the legislative process.
* Strong voting power for the Emperor, Prince-Elector, Archbishop-Elector, and Imperial Prince * Free Imperial City and Imperial Peasant Republic have no voting power * Minor ecclesiastical roles like Imperial Prelate, Primas Germaniae, and Legatus Natus have limited power
policies.name: Early Imperial Diet

desc:
The Bicameral Imperial Diet expands representation by granting voting rights to ecclesiastical dignitaries and princely rulers alike, forming two chambers within the Diet.
* Standard power for Emperor, Prince-Elector, Archbishop-Elector, and Imperial Prince * Imperial Prelate gain meaningful influence * Free Imperial City and Imperial Peasant Republic still lack representation
policies.name: Bicameral Imperial Diet

desc:
With the Tricameral Imperial Diet, Free Imperial City finally gain a decisive voice. The Imperial Diet now consists of three chambers — ecclesiastical, princely, and civic — reflecting a more inclusive balance of power.
* Balanced power among Emperor, Prince-Elector, Archbishop-Elector, Imperial Prince, Free Imperial City, and minor theocratic roles * Imperial Peasant Republic gain the highest influence here * Most inclusive form of the Diet
policies.name: Tricameral Imperial Diet

desc: The Court Assembly is an ancient system, and therefore many of its stipulations and procedures are very outdated. It is time to rework it and establish a proper Imperial Diet that better protects the diverse interests of all members of the Holy Roman Empire.
entities.name: Imperial Diet

desc: This policy ensures the continuous operation of the Examination System as it has been for the centuries prior.
policies.name: Continuous Operation

desc: The abolishment of the Examination System is going to halt social mobility and will directly benefit those who are currently in power. Instead of meritocratic approach, new bureaucrats will be decided through personal, often corrupt, recommendations.
policies.name: Abolish the Examination System

desc: Those wishing to enter the civil service and advance as government officials must take a series of examinations testing their knowledge of Confucian literature and statecraft.
entities.name: Examination System

desc: The virtues and values of traditional Catholicism dictate life within the Holy Roman Empire.
policies.name: Imperial Religion - Catholicism

desc: The The Reformation has changed our views on religion forever, making way for Lutheranism to become the religion of the Empire.
policies.name: Imperial Religion - Lutheranism

desc: The Western Schism has exposed the world to the Hussitism teachings which now dominate the Imperial life.
policies.name: Imperial Religion - Hussitism

desc: Our faith in Calvinism is strong, and should be a foundational part of the Empire from now on. It is therefore our sacred calling to follow Calvinism teachings.
policies.name: Imperial Religion - Calvinism

desc: The finer matters of religion are no longer of such importance. All of Christianity shall be embraced as the religion of the Empire, no matter the sect.
policies.name: Imperial Religion - Christianity

desc: The very foundations of the Holy Roman Empire are built on religious beliefs.
entities.name: Imperial Religion

desc: The Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire can only be worn by male rulers.
policies.name: Agnatic Succession

desc: The gender of our ruler is irrelevant. Female rulers may wear the Imperial Crown of the Holy Roman Empire as rightfully as their male counterparts.
policies.name: Pragmatic Sanction

desc: The succession of the Holy Roman Empire is a delicate matter. The right of succession to the Imperial Throne is prescribed in the Imperial Laws.
entities.name: Imperial Succession

desc: To prevent any single ruler from consolidating power, the Empire enforces a rotation system that actively discourages re-election of incumbents.
policies.name: Rotating Emperorship

desc: Electors are fully independent in choosing the next Emperor. Self-voting is permitted.
policies.name: Free Electorate

desc: Electors favor candidates belonging to the Emperor's dynasty, consolidating dynastic power over the electoral system.
policies.name: Emperor Dynastic Preference

desc: The Emperor promotes the candidacy of their own successor. Imperial policy begins to favor dynastic continuity.
policies.name: Emperor Successor Preference

desc: The elective monarchy is abolished. The Empire becomes a fully hereditary monarchy, solidifying dynastic rule at the cost of Imperial legitimacy.
policies.name: Erbkaisertum

desc: The Holy Roman Empire is built upon the principle of Imperial election. The nature of that election defines the balance of power in the Empire.
entities.name: Imperial Voting

desc: The mark of the Holy See carries unprecedented influence throughout the Catholicism world. By making the gravitas and authority of the Rome a driving force behind our state's religious policies, we will accelerate the conversion of the non-believers while maintaining general social order.
policies.name: Papal Control

desc: For too long, heretics in our realm have enjoyed the same protections and privileges as the faithful. It is time to establish local courts with the authority to prosecute those who refuse our faith, regardless of the consequences to social harmony.
policies.name: Local Courts

desc: The Inquisition is a matter for the state to oversee, not the Rome nor local authorities. State-selected Inquisitors hold the power to spy on all suspected enemies of the realm and subsequently to bring charges against them.
policies.name: State Inquisitors

desc: A central body of Jewish Authority, this council is in charge of religious and judicial affairs with an aim of spreading religious tolerance and protect its people from persecution.
policies.name: Council of Three Lands

desc: Our chief weapon is surprise! Surprise and fear... Our two weapons are fear and surprise... and ruthless efficiency!
policies.name: Spanish Inquisition

desc: Originally established to combat the heresy of Catharism, the Inquisition has become the Catholicism Church's primary tool for investigating and prosecuting heresy. Via specialized ecclesiastical courts, trained inquisitors investigate potential heretics, extract confessions of religious or moral transgression, and impose punishments ranging from penance to execution, for violating Catholic mores.
entities.name: Inquisition Law

desc: The Slavophiles stress the importance of Orthodoxy, Communalism, preservation of traditional values and critique of materialism, individualism and the superficial nature of Western culture. They favor a more isolated path to preserve a unique cultural and spiritual heritage.
policies.name: Slavophiles

desc: The Westernizers value closer ties with Europe and believe that all should align themselves with Western culture. The adoption of Western ideas, institutions, and technologies must take precedence to allow for rapid modernization, industrialization, and social reforms. Concepts such as cultural identity and religious unity hold little value.
policies.name: Westernizers

desc: The ideological perspectives of the nineteenth century divides man to such extent that entire movements emerge, each stemming from the apparent discord among different philosophical, political, and cultural viewpoints.
entities.name: Intellectual Movements

desc: Our potential enemies are many, while friends are hard to come by. It is crucial for the safety of the state that our spies counter any secretive foreign threats within our borders.
policies.name: Home Security

desc: Many sovereigns assume their biggest threats are external. However, our own population could easily bring about the downfall of the government. A strong secret police that keeps a watchful eye on powerful members of our society is necessary to maintain unbroken authority at the top.
policies.name: Secret Police

desc: The ''Jǐnyīwèi'', or 'Embroidered Uniform Guard', is the personal protection force of our ruler. It has full allowance to overrule judicial proceedings when prosecuting state enemies. Not even our ruler's own family members are safe from their reach!
policies.name: Jǐnyīwèi

desc: The ''Oprichniki'', or 'Men aside', are a secret police force sworn to persecute any dangerous entity within our state. They are unswervingly loyal to the ruler, and their actions make them infamous among the civilians — an excellent deterrent for aberrant behavior.
policies.name: Oprichnik

desc: Information is a weapon in its own right. In order to always stay one step ahead of our enemies, it is of great importance to establish a network of spies and informants in our service.
policies.name: Spy Office

desc: The ''Cabinet Noir'', or 'Black Room', is responsible for reconnaissance, conducting espionage in foreign lands, and protecting the ruler from internal and external threats.
policies.name: Cabinet Noir

desc: The Secretnoye Byuro aims to punish Nobles convicted of political crimes, although occasionally it takes on cases of an apolitical nature. Punishments inflicted on those convicted are often made very painful and horrific, in order to dissuade critique towards the ruling regime.
policies.name: Secretnoye Byuro

desc: The interests of our own estates have to come first before the external pressure and influences propagated by China.
policies.name: Limit Chinese Court Influence

desc: The intelligence agency is an organization within the state which conducts spycraft activities such as espionage, cryptography, and providing security from internal threats.
entities.name: Intelligence Agency

desc: The Patriarchs should work together for the greater benefit of the Church as a whole, even if each one of them retains the full authority of their Patriarchy.
policies.name: Cooperation Between Patriarchs

desc: The Patriarchs have full authority over their own Patriarchies, and thus can decide independently the best course of action for them without the need of any discussion with the other Patriarchs.
policies.name: Independent Acting Patriarchs

desc: Despite the different Patriarchs being autonomous in their decisions and not reporting to any higher authority, they are still part of the same faith. It is thus inevitable and even necessary to have some interaction and common discussions.
entities.name: Interpatriarchal Relations

desc: Effectively collecting property taxes is the backbone of our national economy. Despite what the Commoners might advocate for, this revenue is vital for funding various projects, endeavors, and campaigns. As such, the accumulation of revenue and the general administration thereof should be entrusted to methodical Iqṭā' holders.
policies.name: Tax Farming

desc: The ''Jāgir'' system grants land and the right to collect taxes to appointees of the state, known as ''Jagirdars''. Over the decades since its inception, the system has evolved so that the ruling body retains administrative and military authority, while Jagirdars collect taxes and turn over a portion of that revenue to the treasury.
policies.name: Jāgir Taxation

desc: Administrating the vast lands under our jurisdiction is no simple matter. Let us strive to bring the territories closer to our central authority by reasserting our possession of these lands, in spite of protests from the Commoners.
policies.name: Land Acquisition

desc: Our people, regardless of their origin and faith, have long suffered under the taxation of the local ''Muqṭi'''. Let us give them a helping hand by reducing their tax burden.
policies.name: Lenient Taxation

desc: ''Iqṭā''' is the Islam practice of 'tax farming': collecting land revenues from the Commoners as part of ''Zakāh'', the giving of alms, which Islam states generally collect to form their base income.
entities.name: Iqṭā'

desc: By banning alcohol for any citizens in our realm, we can properly ensure the loyalty of the servants of our faith, even if it angers our populace.
policies.name: Ban on Alcohol

desc: Instead of banning alcohol for our people, it would be instead preferable to keep it unrestricted for any of our citizens, ensuring the loyalty of the masses.
policies.name: No Restrictions on Alcohol

desc: In order to balance out the religious duties of the servants of our faith, and the desires of our people, we must decide if the consumption alcohol is allowed or not.
entities.name: Alcohol Restrictions

desc: The Banner army has served us dutifully, delivering blows to our enemies and securing crucial victories. If we are to maintain their top form and discipline, we must reform and improve them, or they will be at risk of decadence.
policies.name: Revise the Jakūn Gūsa

desc: The Jakūn Gūsa served well when on the northern steppes, but as part of the Middle Kingdom they would need to be integrated into the Chinese system.
policies.name: Chinese Jakūn Gūsa

desc: Serving mainly as our military, the Eight Banners system also function as the basis of the organization of society in the Middle Kingdom. Their role should be clearly defined, so that they do not lose their focus.
entities.name: Jakūn Gūsa

desc: Our samurai have a clear model to follow for self-improvement, and they are obligated to abide by it.
policies.name: Enforced Buke Shohatto

desc: The Buke Shohatto is considered a set of general guidelines rather than hard rules, and serves as a romantic ideal to emulate rather than a strict code to obey.
policies.name: Buke Shohatto Guidelines

desc: A series of edicts defining the proper behavior of the samurai. They are designed to inspire the samurai to improve themselves.
entities.name: Buke Shohatto

desc: Free from outside influences, our territory is sure to improve its productivity and economic growth.

mods.label: Foreigners Banned from Imports and Exports

policies.name: Sakoku

desc: With our borders open to the world, both trade and new ideas can flow freely through through.
policies.name: Opened the Country

desc: Japan has always had the luxury of being separated from other countries by the sea. This distance makes closing our borders to the outside world very easy.
entities.name: Overseas Interaction

desc: This reform aims at refining the process behind the selection of candidates and potential bureaucrats during the Imperial Examination. Introducing new formats of tests and holding candidates to higher standards will certainly benefit our administration.
policies.name: New Kējǔ Formats

desc: The classical texts of Confucianism and Daoism have served as the basis of the Kējǔ Examination for centuries. Such historical traditions are not to be broken lightly.
policies.name: Focus on Classics

desc: Being a learned individual does not necessarily mean that someone is apt for government work. Direct appointment of people suited for the task will be more efficient.
policies.name: Direct Appointment

desc: The bureaucrats taking the Imperial exams shall not only be tested on their skills in statecraft, but on their archery and horsemanship as well.
policies.name: Introduce Martial Examination

desc: The Imperial Examination system aims to identify the best and most educated candidates to serve in our bureaucracy. This will ensure that only the brightest minds in our nation are the ones turning the wheels of the administration, and thus that they turn smoothly.
entities.name: Kējǔ Examination

desc: The leadership of Sikhism would lay on the Khalsa as a whole, which would serve as its Gurū.
policies.name: Guru Panth

desc: Only by organizing the military forces of the Khalsa into a mighty army will they will be able to serve their function as protectors of Sikhism.
policies.name: Khalsa Fauj

desc: The members of the Khalsa are not just brutes thrown to fight, but refined individuals who uphold the rites of initiation and the rules of conduct and dress code placed upon them as members of the community. The prestige of the Khalsa is not on the might of its warriors but on the appeal of their purity.
policies.name: Amrit Sanskar

desc: A warrior community tasked with the defense of Sikhism and its followers, its rules of conduct and initiation will set a standard for all the faithful.
entities.name: Khalsa

desc: The means of transaction might as well be conducted by barter.
policies.name: Barter Economy

desc: Our attempts to make use of metal currencies have been rather ineffective due to our lack of resources. Perhaps now we will be able to change the course.
policies.name: Metal Coinage

desc: In order to stimulate the economy, let us found a new Paper currency, the Jeohwa. It will also allow us to pivot towards the Capital Economy.
policies.name: Jeohwa

desc: Instead of spending our efforts and resources on maintaining our own currency, we could rely on imported foreign coins of China.
policies.name: Chinese Currency

desc: A focus on different types of currencies is bound to shape our country in many diverse ways, not just economically, but socially as well.
entities.name: Dominant Currency

desc: 'Might makes right' accurately describes the current practical politics of the Holy Roman Empire; disputes between our members will be resolved on the battlefield.
policies.name: Absence of Landfriede

desc: The ''Landfriede'', or 'land peace,' is a decree which dictates that disputes between members of the Holy Roman Empire must be settled in the Imperial Court rather than on the battlefield. This mandate helps us stay cohesive as an empire, rather than becoming weak through petty in-fighting.
policies.name: Institute the Landfriede

desc: The ''Landfriede'' gains additional influence and recognition amongst members of the Holy Roman Empire.
policies.name: Expand the Landfriede

desc: The ''Landfriede'' is now a powerful institution. Members of the Holy Roman Empire greatly respect its authority.
policies.name: Empower the Landfriede

desc: The ''Landfriede'' is at its apex of influence and power within the Holy Roman Empire, and private warfdare between member states has been permanently outlawed. Any disputes that arise are subject to judgment in the Imperial Court.
policies.name: Ewiger Landfriede

desc: Restrict the capabilities of the members of the Holy Roman Empire and effectively outlaws warfare within the Empire.
policies.name: Outlaw Internal Warfare

desc: The ''Landfriede'', or 'land peace,' is a decree which dictates that disputes between members of the Holy Roman Empire must be settled in the Imperial Court rather than on the battlefield. This mandate helps us stay cohesive as an empire, rather than becoming weak through petty in-fighting.
entities.name: Landfriede

desc: By obfuscating everyday legal processes behind the prestigious language only used by the Crown, the rabble cannot so easily interfere in matters of state.
policies.name: Court Language

desc: By clarifying everyday legal process into the common tongue, ordinary folk become less likely to run afoul of the law.
policies.name: Common Language

desc: By giving equal rights to all the languages of our realm, we ensure the support of the Commoners and the stability of the realm.
policies.name: Multi-Lingual Court

desc: The customs of our social hierarchy and legal proceedings must be concisely and uniformly written down in the language we find most appropriate.
entities.name: Language of Pleading

desc: Conversion policies from the Kingdom of Rome have largely been ignored in order to form a peaceful coexistence with the local Orthodoxy populace.
policies.name: Tolerance of the Orthodoxy Faith

desc: Reconversion policies from the Kingdom of Rome towards the Orthodoxy are insituted in the legal code of the Empire of Constantinople, but are not enforced.
policies.name: Limited Reconversion Efforts

desc: Reconversion policies towards the Orthodoxy populace are heavily enforced with the full backing of the Kingdom of Rome.
policies.name: Sanctioned Reconversion Efforts

desc: In order to garner support for restoring the Empire of Constantinople, a compromise was reached with the Kingdom of Rome regarding strengthening Catholicism supremacy over the local Orthodoxy branch.
entities.name: Orthodoxy Status within the Empire of Constantinople

desc:
There are a plethora of informal punitive systems developed by communities based on their customs, traditions, and values. These legal systems have been passed down orally from generation to generation and are deeply rooted in the culture and history of the community.

The strength of Traditional Law lies in its ability to reflect the unique needs and values of a particular community. It is based on a shared understanding of what is right and wrong, and is often seen as more legitimate and accessible than formal legal systems. However, it can also be limited by its insularity and lack of flexibility.
policies.name: Traditional Law

desc: Gustavus Adolphus founded the first Swedish court of appeals, 'Svea Hovrätt', in 1614 as a higher instance than the old local courts, or 'tingsrätt'. Today there are six such courts in Sweden.
policies.name: Court of Appeals

desc: Civil Law, a legal system with roots in ancient Rome, is known for its precise written codification of laws and regulations. However, the rigidity of its structure can hinder the adaptation required to address the evolving needs of the people. Nonetheless, Civil Law can bring peace and stability to even the most turbulent nation.
policies.name: Civil Law

desc: Common Law is a legal system that originated amongst the Anglo-Saxon kingdoms. It is characterized by a reliance on precedent; judges are bound by their previous decisions rather than strict adherence to the written law of the state. This allows for a degree of predictability and consistency in legal decisions, but can also make it difficult to adapt to changing circumstances and may lead to the entrenchment of unjust or outdated laws.
policies.name: Common Law

desc: Uniquely blending pastoral traditions and legal norms, the Vlach Law encapsulates a distinct system governing Romanian communities across medieval Europe. It affirms the rights to travel, bear arms, and practice hunting while sparing them from mandatory labor for landowners, instead paying taxes in livestock or coin. Furthermore, it institutes a binding military service commitment tailored to each realm, creating a network of Romanian and legal heritage.
policies.name: Vlach Law

desc: Sharī'ah Law is a comprehensive and deeply entrenched legal system in Islamic countries that governs many aspects of life, from personal conduct to matters of state. It has provided stability and continuity for centuries, but its strict and sometimes harsh penalties can be controversial and divisive.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Liturgical Language

policies.name: Sharī'ah Law

desc: Codify the traditional customs of the realm, recognizing inheritance through the female line while allowing [
policies.name: Matrilineal Customary Law

desc: Pyrenean Law is a legal system native to the peoples living around the Pyrenean Mountains. Despite the fact that this law was influenced by both the Civil Law and the Gothic Law, it remained different from them. Based on traditional customs and practices, this legal system is so embedded in our culture than rulers are obliogated to adapt to it, rather than overriding it with their own systems.
policies.name: Pyrenean Law

desc: This was the legal code of Kievan Rus', heavily influenced by their Norse origins. It has been rewritten many times over the centuries since its inception, and is the main source of Old Russian Law.
policies.name: Russkaya Pravda

desc: The Pskov Judicial Charter is the Old Russian legal code which was built on the Russkaya Pravda. It emcompasses many important features of the political, social, and economic life within Pskov.
policies.name: Pskov Judicial Charter

desc: The Novgorod Judicial Charter is an Old Russian legal code which codifies many common practices within Novgorod. It also sets and defines the four positions in the Novgorodian court and covers the administrative matters of the state.
policies.name: Novgorod Judicial Charter

desc: The 'Upper Bavarian Land Rights' is a collection of old Bavarian legal codes which codifies many common practices within Bavaria. It also sets and defines the role of the Nobility in Bavaria's court and covers administrative matters of the state.
policies.name: Upper Bavarian Land Rights

desc: Welsh Law, also known as ''Cyfraith Hywel'', is a unique legal system that emerged from the ancient customs of Wales. It differs from both Common Law and Civil Law in that it emphasizes restorative justice, placing a greater emphasis on compensation and reconciliation rather than punishment. The law was created by the Welsh kings and princes to promote unity and order among the Welsh people, and is known for its complexity and adherence to precedent.
policies.name: Cyfraith Hywel

desc: The ''Fetha Negest'', or Justice of the Kings, is a theocratic legal code compiled by Abu'l-Fada'il ibn al-Assal, and is a significant work of justice. Drawing from apostolic writings and Byzantine law codes, it encompasses ecclesiastical and secular matters, and is further influenced by Roman law.
policies.name: Fetha Negest

desc: A set of legal frameworks aimed at curbing the power of influential Nobility that do not align themselves with the agenda of our central authority. These sets of jurisprudence aim at pushing back against a powerful noble class.
policies.name: Ordinances of Justice

desc: A body of aristocrats and various classes of citizens, including Burghers and artisans as well as bankers, the ''Consiglio Maggiore'' is in charge of the autocratic apparatus within our Republic.
policies.name: Consiglio Maggiore

desc: A set of laws and articles, drafted to greatly curb the power of the Nobility. The code entails the passing of noble property to the state in certain circumstances, as well as limiting the arbitrary powers of the Nobility throughout our realm.
policies.name: Maiestas Carolina

desc: Byzantine law, evolving from Roman law with Christian and Hellenistic influence, largely derives from Justinian's ''Corpus Juris Civilis'', which emphasizes ceremonial emperor roles, and reflects philosophical and religious ideals.
policies.name: Byzantine Law

desc: A compendium of translated Greek Byzantine books of law and great works of ancient philosophy into the Serbian language, issued by Emperor Ser Stefan Dusan.
policies.name: Law of the Pious Emperor

desc: The Goryeon Code, also known as ''Gyeongje Yukjeon'' - ''Six Codes of Governance'' - is the code of law of Korea. Shaped by the Chinese bureaucratic arts, this code has prevailed in our state for centuries.
policies.name: Goryeon Code

desc: The Joseon Code, also known as ''Gyeongguk Daejeon'' - ''National Code'' - is the revision of the old Goryeon Code. With the founding of a new dynasty, many laws and traditions of the previous code have been compiled anew in the current code.
policies.name: Joseon Code

desc: The Great Code shall be created to address all the critical problems that our dynasty faces and the ones that our predecessors faced. It will ensure that we will not fall to corruption and ministerial abuses of power!
policies.name: The Great Code

desc: The College of Justice has reformed our Civil Law towards a new standard. This Institution consists of well-educated members of our country, who will rule on any important topic concerning the ''Scots Law''.
policies.name: Scottish Civil Law

desc: The Sobornoye Ulozheniye serves as a foundational legal and social code that adapts the laws to fit a country with a strong centralized state and a clear social hierarchy. It builds upon the prevalent code and incorporates certain elements from the Byzantine code of law, solidifying class distinctions, and codifying a legal system that reflects the prevailing political and religious influences of the time.
policies.name: Sobornoye Ulozheniye

desc: A set of statutes that shape our legislation and offer a robust frame for the future of our people, these statutes are comprehensive and extremely influential. Their jurisdiction impacts various aspects of our society, from private to public law and the responsibilities of each social class.
policies.name: Piotrków-Wiślica Statutes

desc: The legal Codes of Jutland, Zealand, and Scania grants us regional legal systems. While prone to regionalism, it will represent the will of the Danish people.
policies.name: Regional Laws of Denmark

desc: A unified legal code for our country will bring a new standardized legal framework for our government to work in and our subjects to appeal to.
policies.name: Danske Lov

desc: This set of laws provides the legal framework for our activities and subjects in the colonial territories. It is especially concerned with the rights of the native population and their organization into the encomiendas system.
policies.name: Laws of Burgos

desc: The New Laws serve as an improved version building upon the Laws of Burgos, strengthening the control that we can assert in our colonial possessions.
policies.name: Leyes Nuevas

desc: The ''Siete Partidas'' is a compilation of statutory laws made by Alfonso X of Castile with the intention of uniformizing the legislation of his realm. It focuses on legislative issues, but also moral ones.
policies.name: Siete Partidas

desc: The Ordenamiento de Alcalá is a legal code that unifies and centralizes our diverse laws, asserting central authority over local customs and privileges.
policies.name: Ordenamiento de Alcalá

desc: A series of codified laws aimed at confirming the legal responsibilities and framework of the elites, as well as promoting a wave of centralization.
policies.name: Statutes of Lithuania

desc: To combat the lack of a code within the nation, as well as the criminal activity conducted by those of the higher strata, the Sudebnik of Lithuania was writen in order to properly rein in the chaos, as well as give more power to the Crown.
policies.name: Sudebnik of Lithuania

desc: The Articles of Agreement are the cornerstone of the social order on board a pirate ship. They guarantee that every crewman has an equal vote in all matters and an equal share of all plunder. Articles such as these should be established for the republic itself, so that the liberty and equality of all pirates is secured.
policies.name: Articles of Agreement

desc: A collection of legislations that together make up the laws of Ottomans, focused on providing internal stability for the numerous ethnicities rather than on conquering new lands.
policies.name: kanun‐i Osmani

desc: The Royal Ordinances are a set of statutes issued to regulate various aspects of the royal court and household. These rules outline the roles and responsibilities of court officials and include detailed provisions for the coronation ceremony of Aragonese kings.
policies.name: Aragonese Royal Ordinances

desc: Although secret from the public, the Mongol Law aimed for three things: obedience to the current ruler, binding together the people, and severely punishing any wrongdoing to the state. By keeping it secret from the public it can also be more easily changed to suit any other needs.
policies.name: Mongol Law

desc: A new compilation of the numerous laws within our realm, they will allow us to properly centralize and ensure control over our territories.
policies.name: Nueva Recopilación

desc: The codified customs of the Duchy of Normandy emphasize feudal land rights, noble privilege, and local autonomy. While favoring a decentralized and traditional society, these laws form a robust legal framework that ensures the power of the nobility and preserves the distinct identity of the Normandy.
policies.name: Coutume de Normandie

desc: The great compilation of Roman law, ordered under Emperor Justinian, gathered centuries of rulings, edicts, and wisdom into a single body. The Codex, Digest, Institutes, and Novellae together have once again become the backbone of governance and justice, ensuring our authority, legal consistency, and the proper conduct of our government.
policies.name: Corpus Juris Civilis

desc: The Assizes of Romania codifies Francien feudal law within the Latin East, establishing a rigid hierarchy between the rulers and their vassal lords. It empoweres the High Court to mediate disputes over fiefs and military service while enforcing a dual social system that keeps the Greek peasantry in semi-servitude. This legal framework provides the structural continuity that allows the Frankokratia to endure as a Latin-governed society.
policies.name: Assizes of Romania

desc: Emerging from the Giudicato of Arborea, this is one of the first comprehensive legal codes in Europe written in a Romance vernacular (Sardinian). It establishes a culture of 'Rule of Law' that protects the rights of commoners and regulates pastoral land use. This legal sophistication allows the Sardinians to maintain a unified social fabric. It fosters a cultural identity defined by civic rights and a deep-seated respect for the collective ownership of the ''Logu''.
policies.name: Carta de Logu

desc: For as long as people have gathered together in societies, they have created laws to govern their actions and interactions. Legal codes are a reflection of the values and beliefs of a society, shaping everything from how people conduct business to how they treat each other. They are the very fabric that holds a society together, providing a framework for order and justice. Despite their differences, people tend to share a common goal: to create a just and fair society where everyone can live in peace and prosperity.
entities.name: Legal Code

desc: No legal framework will be set.
policies.name: No Legal Framework

desc: A basic framework will be set.
policies.name: Basic Legal Framework

desc: A Chinese bureaucratic system will be set.
policies.name: Sinicized Legal Framework

desc: This law lays out the legal framework employed by our bureaucracy.
entities.name: Bureaucratic Law

desc: The state is above morals; above virtues and sins. The government must make decisions purely based on the beneficial gains for the state - even if they are deemed as evil. As such, the sovereign has the right to act for the benefit of the state without moral consideration.
policies.name: Machiavellian Reign

desc: Absolute rule of a single monarch is as detrimental to the state as letting the masses rule themselves. The power of the monarch should not be subject to any faction within the state, though to some extent it should be limited by institutions to maintain a balance of power between ruler and the people.
policies.name: ''Les Six Livres de la République''

desc:
The nature of humanity is characterized by reason and tolerance. No man is born evil. However, human nature leads our people to be selfish and act only for their own good.
The government ensures that this selfishness is resolved in civil ways. It also serves to defend the natural rights of life, health, liberty, and possession.
policies.name: ''Two Treatises of Government''

desc:
Life without civilization, also called the state of nature, is anarchy. Every man is for himself, and a war of all against all is the only outcome possible without an absolute centralized authority to keep it all in check.
Our people cede many rights to our sovereign authority for the sake of protection from utter decimation.
policies.name: ''Leviathan''

desc:
The social contract is a concept wherein legitimate government arises from a mutual agreement among individuals to come together and form civil society.
While certain limitations are put on the natural freedoms of people within that society, they are ceded in exchange for the security and benefits provided by the state.
policies.name: The Social Contract

desc: The concepts of individualism and freedom have evolved significantly over the centuries, and older ideals differ greatly from modern interpretations. Our state can best secure the individual liberties and freedom of our people by synthesizing contemporary wisdom with that of the past.
policies.name: Liberty of the Ancients vs. the Moderns

policy_names: Liberty of the Ancients vs. the Moderns

desc: A monarchy can only survive as long as its subjects believe in the legitimacy of their ruler. There are many ways in which rulers justify their power. As time goes on, new political philosophies will arise which explain the need for a strong government in their own ways.
entities.name: Legitimization of Power

desc: By adhering to practices popularized by Byzantine priests, we can borrow some of the legitimacy of their faiths.
policies.name: Byzantine Rites

desc: Emphasize our own local rites over others.
policies.name: Local Rites

desc: Introduce rites such as mass, sacraments and liturgy of the hours, in adjacency to the Catholicism practices.
policies.name: Catholicism-Influenced Rites

desc: Various worship practices centered around hymns, readings and rites.
entities.name: Liturgical Practices

desc: Administration will be handled at a tribal level, with each tribal leader making the decisions for their group.
policies.name: Tribal Administration

desc: Administration will be handled at a confederation level, with the leader directing our people.
policies.name: Sinicized Administration

desc: This law defines the way our people will be administered.
entities.name: Administration Law

desc: Ireland was originally conquered by Anglo-Norman knights looking to seize some personal land and glory. However, the royal seat is impotent.

mods.label: Can Use Lordship of Ireland Casus Belli

policies.name: Laudabiliter

desc: Ordinances enforcing continental customs in Ireland, through banning Celtic dress and intermarriage, to keep the settler community distinct and dominant.
policies.name: Statutes of Kilkenny

desc: We may enforce members of the Lordship to convert to our religion.
policies.name: Religious Ascendancy

desc: The shape of rule in Ireland can be as wild as the great Atlantic crashing against the craggy cliffs, or as steadfast as the bogs.
entities.name: Rule of Ireland

desc: Confucianism is a philosophy developed from the teachings of Confucius, or Kǒng Fūzǐ, emphasizing social harmony and the righteousness of government institutions.
policies.name: Confucianism

desc: Daoism is a philosophy emphasizing living in harmony with the ''Dào'', the living force of the universe, and the concept of ''Wúwéi'', or 'action with no-action'.
policies.name: Daoism

desc: Pure Land Buddhism is one of the most followed schools of East Asian Buddhism, and is centered around the idea of achieving rebirth in a Buddha's Pure Land. The most common Pure Land is that of the Buddha Amitābha, and the most important teachings are the ''Three Pure Land Sutras''. The principal form of practice is the mindfulness of the Buddha, via repeating the name of the Buddha as a form of recitation.
policies.name: Pure Land Buddhism

desc: The Lotus School, so named to honor the importance of the ''Lotus Sutra'', is one of the earliest Buddhist schools developed in China. It emphasizes the doctrine of the ''One Vehicle'', promoting an inclusive view and understanding of all Buddhist teachings.
policies.name: Lotus School

desc: Called ''Wéishí'' or ''Fǎxiàng'' in China, and ''Hossō'' in Japan, the Dharma School tradition emerged from India and has had a profound influence on Eastern Buddhism. It focuses on idealism and the idea that reality is only consciousness, and emphasizes the practices of yoga and meditation.
policies.name: Dharma School

desc: Taking its name from the ''Flower Garland Sutra'', and called ''Huáyán'' in China, ''Kegon'' in Japan, and ''Hwaeom'' in Korea, Flower Garland School is one of the main Buddhist traditions developed in China. It emphasizes the doctrine of interpenetration, wherein all things exist in a state of mutual dependence and are simultaneously present within each other.
policies.name: Flower Garland School

desc: The Meditation School was founded by Bodhidharma, according to tradition, and is called ''Chán'' in China, ''Zen'' in Japan, ''Seon'' in Korea and ''Thiền'' in Vietnam. Though meditation is a general practice in Buddhism, this school emphasizes its use as a means of achieving enlightenment, usually in a sitting position, but also while performing physical activities like martial arts.
policies.name: Meditation School

desc: The Mantra School, called ''Zhēnyán'' in China and ''Shingon'' in Japan, focuses on the esoteric practices of Vajrayāna, especially those called the 'three mysteries': mudra, mantra, and mandala. Its practices have been very influential in the development of many other schools of Buddhism.
policies.name: Mantra School

desc: Emerging as a syncretism of mixed practices from Buddhism, Shintō, and Onmyōdō, Shugendō aims for the achievement of supernatural powers via religious training in the mountains. Mountain worship and trekking are the main focuses of this sect, as well as other esoteric practices and rituals.
policies.name: Shugendō

desc: When Tantric Buddhist practices came into Yúnnán, they mixed with traditions of Chinese, Tibetan, and Burmese origin, creating a hybrdized faith. As such, Azhaliism has emerged as a relatively localized tradition, similar yet distinct from the other, bigger schools.
policies.name: Azhaliism

desc: Centered around the worship of deities and ancestral spirits, Musok beliefs have been present in Korea since before the introduction of Buddhism. Even after that, its beliefs, practices, and rituals continue to be an important part of the region's culture.
policies.name: Musok

desc: One of the earliest Buddhist schools in India, the traditions of Mūlasarvāstivāda have almost disappeared from most currents of Buddhism, only surviving in Tibetan Buddhism and in Indonesia. There, the first current to arrive was Hīnayāna, and the Mūlasarvāstivāda, together with Tantric Practices, became prominent during the Śrīvijaya Empire.
policies.name: Mūlasarvāstivāda

desc: A center of Buddhist scholarship since the religion first arrived on the island, Sailan has developed its own tradition of Theravāda Buddhism. As such, it has been influential in the development and spread of Buddhism in other neighboring areas, especially since the start of the decline of Buddhism in mainland India.
policies.name: Mahāvihāra

desc: Although strongly influenced by the Mahāvihāra Buddhism of Sailan, other forms of Buddhism have spread around Burma. Eastern Buddhism and Theravāda traditions, as well as Hinduism and also some remnants of pre-Buddhism beliefs, have all blended together, giving rise to a particular flavor of Theravāda. While very similar to the one practiced in Sailan, this sect also incorporates many elements of Eastern Buddhism and other esoteric traditions.
policies.name: Burmese Buddhism

desc: Many different forms of Buddhism have been present in the lands of Thai people for ages, from Chinese-influenced Eastern Buddhism to earlier Indian Buddhist traditions. Eventually, the Theravāda tradition from Sailan became the main school of thought, but influence from earlier traditions and even from Thai folk beliefs still remain.
policies.name: Lankavong

desc: The first form of Buddhism that entered the Khmer area was Eastern Buddhism, with strong Tantric influence, which replaced the Hindu beliefs already present in the region. Over time, Theravāda replaced Eastern Buddhism, and a great shift was made towards monastic life.
policies.name: Khmer Buddhism

desc: The main current of philosophy and teachings that form the core beliefs of a sect.
entities.name: Main Philosophy

desc: By focusing on elevating the Mamālīk that serve the Sultan, we will ensure that our elite troops remain disciplined and effective.
policies.name: Al-Mamālik al-Sulṭāniyya

desc: The Mamālīk that serve under the Amir class are a great source of able-bodied men to supplement our frontlines.
policies.name: Mamālik al-Umarā'

desc: An army cannot properly function without robust auxiliary troops and solid supply lines.
policies.name: Ajnād al-Ḥalqa

desc: Despite the strict conversion and manumission that older Mamālīk went through, they seem to always attempt to undermine central authority. A new corps must be raised, whose men are trained and taught in a different way.
policies.name: Awlād al-Nās

desc: The heart of our stratocratic administration is none other than the army. By drafting laws and stipulations to carefully form it, we will defend our people efficiently against outside threats.
entities.name: Mamlūk Army Law

desc: Promotion based on merit is a great way to accumulate talented and strong warriors regardless of their position and background.
policies.name: Merit Basis

desc: By giving priority to soldiers who are culturally homogenous, we can have a tightly-knitted army that shares a common pride.
policies.name: Origin Basis

desc: The military offices of our army can be passed down from father to son, signifying a continuity in the legitimacy of the throne.
policies.name: Dynastic Basis

desc: The legalities that premiate promotion within our military ranks are an important cornerstone of our country.
entities.name: Mamlūk Promotion Law

desc: By adopting a rigid hierarchy, we will ensure that all recruits and members of the Mamālīk focus on mastering their craft instead of chasing a promotion.
policies.name: Rigid

desc: A fluid system of ranks would only result in our soldiers feeling part of our military forces. The appeal of growth and scaling the hierarchy of a military is a great boost for those who rise from poverty or servitude.
policies.name: Fluid

desc: The hierarchy within our military is the framework that makes up the most important institution of our land.
entities.name: Mamlūk Rank System

desc: Not every tree in the forest is suitable for shipbuilding. To ensure our ships are of the very best quality, we will by law require that any felled trees apt for building ships be immediately surrendered for that purpose.
policies.name: Forestry Ordinance

desc: Every coastal settlement shall mandate naval service for their young men, who are to devote a minimum of one year to our fleets.
policies.name: Mandatory Impressment

desc: A fleet in disrepair can be a dangerous disadvantage in times of trouble. We will therefore carry out regular maintenance audits of our main shipyards and ports to ensure our fleet is in perfect shape at all times.
policies.name: Navy Audits

desc: The navy will guard our main trade routes in order to keep pirates and other undesirables away from our commercial fleets.
policies.name: Protect Trade Routes

desc: We will pass a law to create a standard for shipwrights in order to be more efficient when constructing ships.
policies.name: Shipwright Standard Regulation

desc: The Consulate of the Sea is a new quasi-judicial body that will administer maritime and commercial law.
policies.name: Consulate of the Sea

desc: Based on the original Fuero of San Sebastián, the oldest maritime law in Europe, this code applies to every port in our possession and details the rights and duties of their inhabitants.
policies.name: Navarrese Maritime Code

desc: Centuries of maritime wisdom and access to high quality cotton and lumber have given way to a most formidable merchant fleet. Equipped with cutting edge designs and new sail compositions, these vessels are the pride of our people.
policies.name: Kilwan Merchant Navy

desc: A pirate enterprise cannot function without a way to sell their stolen goods. We must ensure that conditions in the Republic are favorable for smuggling operations.
policies.name: Smugglers' Haven

desc: The dominance of our foes must be contested across all our markets. Through strong central directives and preferential mercantilistic practices, we will attempt to give our merchants a clear edge over those of our enemies and rivals.
policies.name: Act of Navigation

desc: Maritime laws, also known as admiralty laws or marine laws, are a specialized set of legal principles and regulations that govern various aspects of maritime activities and commerce. These laws encompass a broad range of matters related to navigation, shipping, trade, and maritime activities taking place on oceans, seas, and other navigable waterways. They cover areas such as maritime contracts, vessel ownership and registration, marine insurance, salvage and wrecks, liability and compensation for maritime accidents, crew rights and responsibilities, and many other aspects that pertain to maritime affairs. Maritime laws are designed to ensure safe, orderly, and fair practices in the maritime industry and resolve disputes that may arise in the context of maritime activities.
entities.name: Maritime Law

desc: Monogamous marriage refers to a cultural or societal practice of union between two individuals, based on established customs, values, and norms.
policies.name: Monogamous Marriage

desc: Nikāḥ in Islamic culture is the solemn and legally binding marriage contract between a man and a woman.
policies.name: Nikāḥ

desc: The Adamite sect rejects the concept of traditional marriage, preferring to live within communal structures without a clear hierarchy.
policies.name: Communal Living

desc: Marriage between a man and multiple women is seen as a sign of wealth and power within many communities.
policies.name: Polygyny

desc: The Díshù System allows the practice of entertaining concubines at court in order to secure heirs.
policies.name: Díshù System

desc: Celibacy refers to the state of abstaining from marriage and sexual relations. It is a choice often tied to religious or personal beliefs, emphasizing a life without a romantic or sexual partner.
policies.name: Celibacy

desc: Marriage law refers to the legal framework that governs the institution of marriage within a particular jurisdiction.
entities.name: Marriage Law

desc: The Hàn Chinese shall be forced to shave the front of the heads, while their hair on the back shall be grown longer and braided to form the Manchu Biànzi.
policies.name: Enforce Biànzi

desc: The Manchu officials will adopt Hànfú, the Hàn Chinese clothing style, to be more in line with the dominant ethnicity of the state.
policies.name: Adoption of the Hànfú

desc: Tìfāyìfú shall be regarded as our cultural policy towards the Chinese. Amongst the chief requirements shall be for the Hàn to organize their hair in the Biànzi style.
entities.name: Tìfāyìfú

desc: Our people will share the burden when there is a call to arms, regardless of their [
policies.name: Inclusive Levies

desc: The Nobility of our country will lead our calls to arms, since they are the most willing and prepared for war.
policies.name: Noble Levies

desc: In the early days of our empire, our army was made up of sixteen clans whose leaders promised to protect the great Mansa and the Malian State. Translated as '''the Sixteen Slaves that carry the Bow''', the Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro are the high Nobility of the country and serve as commanders of the Malian cavalry.
policies.name: Ton-ta-jon-ta-ni-woro

desc: The Commoners make up the bulk of our levies, so we must take care to recruit as many as possible when the need arises.
policies.name: Peasant Levies

desc: On holidays, every man in the country will take up bows and arrows, and practice archery. This will win us high honor in battle, and ensure we profit from our warlike enterprises.
policies.name: Longbow Competitions

desc: Meaning 'All Together', this system of universal military obligation demands that all able-bodied citizens, regardless of age or gender, are expected to defend the homeland when threatened. Unlike professional armies or feudal levies, this mobilizes the entire population to protect their independence, reflecting a communal commitment to defending their nation.
policies.name: Zamanička Vojska

desc: The Paik System is a corvée labor system where capable adults, the so-called ''Paiks'', are obligated to serve in the state militia in exchange for farmland.
policies.name: Paik System

desc: Alarde is a Castilian system of levy recruitment that assigns cities of the realm the annual responsibility of organizing several ''alardes'', a type of military parade used to train troops. This keeps them fit and ready for military campaigns when required.
policies.name: Alarde

desc: Our army is made up mainly of levies that are recruited from certain [
] of our country, who will fight for us until we disband them.
entities.name: Levy Law

desc: Based around the fixed principal Cities of the pastoral herds, this is the foundational organization of the Mesta. Their supervision ensures the security of our pastoral sheep herds of the Merino Breed.
policies.name: Quadrillas Organization

desc: The Right of Possession regulates rent prizes for pasture fields and serves as the legal groundwork for the Mesta sheep herds.
policies.name: Right of Possession

desc: The Mesta Association together with its council protects the rights and interests of the livestock owners in our country.
entities.name: Mesta Council

desc: The size of our court deems it necessary to empower and expand our bureaucratic efforts, should we wish to maintain efficiency and speed.
policies.name: Expand Palace Bureaucracy

desc: Our vast realm rests on the shoulders of a capable bureaucratic system, and a robust basis for our taxation system resides in proper census accounts. To assist the proper conduct of our bureaucracy, we will commence a census across our lands.
policies.name: Conduct Population Census

desc: The wealth of China is often coveted by foreign merchants. It would be wise to institute tariff controls and grasp the flow of goods that enter and exit our borders.
policies.name: Increase Tariff Control

desc: The concepts of a caring administration, capable bureaucrats, and resistance to corruption often depend on one another. Thus, public administration is a form of morality.
policies.name: Issue Great Warnings

desc: Roads are the lifeblood of our continued prosperity. In an effort to connect our distant provinces and facilitate precious merchant activities, we will delve into establishing robust infrastructure networks across our lands.
policies.name: Commence Infrastructure Works

desc: Our fortifications are the key to our survival. We need to maintain them in prime condition, and ensure that all the vulnerable points of our territory are properly fortified.
policies.name: Reinforce Fortifications

desc: Imperial decrees are the key to the well functioning of the Middle Kingdom, ensuring that the authority of the Middle Kingdom gets enforced throughout.
entities.name: Middle Kingdom

desc: None of the estates are obligated to provide the Hre with additional troops.
policies.name: No Military Contribution

desc: The Hre gains the privilege to construct Imperial Armory (Abroad) within the lands of the Empire.
policies.name: Imperial Armory Implementation

desc: Every Imperial Armory (Abroad) shall gain extra resources in order to expand the amount of possible soldiers recruited for the Empire.
policies.name: Expansion of the Armories

desc: With further expansion of available resources for the Imperial Armory (Abroad), the [
] from the Empire shall allow the Hre to create a proper, standing army.
policies.name: Imperial Standing Army

desc: The final legislative level for Imperial Armory (Abroad). Once enacted, the potential of the army under the direct control of the Hre will reach a never-before-seen height.
policies.name: Great Imperial Army

desc: The Imperial Register is a list that specifies the exact number of troops each estate must supply to the Hre.
entities.name: Imperial Register

desc: Control over the mining privileges rests in the hand of the state, allowing for flexible and efficient mining operations.
policies.name: Bergordnung

desc: All rare minerals are directly owned by our ruler, giving them ultimate control over any extraction operations.
policies.name: Direct Control of the Ruler

desc: The Nobility controls all mining operations.
policies.name: Nobility-Controlled Mining Operations

desc: The Burghers control all mining operations.
policies.name: Burghers-Controlled Mining Operations

desc: The Commoners controls all mining operations.
policies.name: Commoner-Controlled Mining Operations

desc: The ''Novo Brdo'' Code provides detailed guidelines on property rights, safety measures, and economic practices, significantly influencing the development and prosperity of our mining communities.
policies.name: Novo Brdo Code

desc: As per the monarch's ancient patrimonial rights, the Crown is entitled to the natural riches of the land. However, such an arrangement would be tyrannical, so this natural right has been reduced to a simple twenty percent tax on all precious metals produced in the country and its colonies.
policies.name: Royal Fifth

desc: This law determines who owns the mining operations in our country.
entities.name: Mining Law

desc: The Non-Possessors believe that the Church should distance itself from material wealth and follow a more monastic and contemplative lifestyle. A rejection of worldly possessions is important if one is to foster a closer relationship with God. The movement is heavily influenced by the teachings of Nil Sorsky.
policies.name: Non-Possessors

desc: The Possessors support Church's ownership of land and property, deeming it necessary for the Church to possess material wealth in order to fulfill its spiritual and social responsibilities. Examples of such commitments are charitable activities, maintaining religious institutions, develop infrastructure and provide education.
policies.name: Possessors

desc: The Possessors and Non-Possessors have different views on the role of wealth within the Church and its impact on the spiritual life of clergy and followers.
entities.name: Monastic Reformation Movement

desc: The empire is in no need of additional gold. Lifting the taxation burdens of its members allows the administration to focus on other tasks instead.
policies.name: No Taxation

desc: While the Hre can open their own coffers to solve many issues, a financial buffer in the form of a proper treasury would allow the current and future emperors to better finance internal affairs in the Holy Roman Empire.
policies.name: Treasury Taxation

desc: The Roman Month is not enough to cover the protection of the Holy Roman Empire. A new tax needs to be established which directly finances the Hre.
policies.name: Direct Taxation

desc: Only the taxation of all our member states can sustain the financial challenges of the Holy Roman Empire.
policies.name: Imperial Taxation

desc: The Holy Roman Empire requires gold to function like any other political entity. A series of tax laws can be applied to siphon gold from the members to ensure financial stability of the Empire.
entities.name: Imperial Tax Law

desc: Members will be not able to be called into defensive wars declared on other members.
policies.name: No Defense

desc: Members will be able to be called into defensive wars declared on other members, but do not have to accept.
policies.name: Possible Defense

desc: Members will automatically be called into defensive wars declared on other members, but do not have to accept.
policies.name: Automatic Defense

desc: Members will automatically join in defensive wars declared on other members.
policies.name: Assured Defense

desc: The policy outlining how members will defend each other in the event of war being declared.
entities.name: Mutual Defense

desc: Members will automatically join in offensive wars declared by other members.
policies.name: Assured Offense

desc: Members will automatically be called into offensive wars declared by other members, but do not have to accept.
policies.name: Automatic Offense

desc: Members will be able to be called into offensive wars declared by other members, but do not have to accept.
policies.name: Possible Offense

desc: Members will be not able to be called into offensive wars declared by other members.
policies.name: No Offense

desc: The policy outlining how members will support each other in the event of them declaring war against another country.
entities.name: Mutual Offense

desc: Our colonial authorities will encourage trade with the native population to start a regular flow of profitable goods into our markets.
policies.name: Trade

desc: Our colonial authorities will attempt to subjugate the native population into a new, profitable source of labor for our country.
policies.name: Subjugation

desc: Our colonial authorities will try to integrate the native population with our own, to make them more self-sufficient and promote social stability.
policies.name: Integration

desc: This establishes the policy that our country will follow regarding the native people inhabiting our colonies.
entities.name: Native Policy

desc: Combat and power are the only ways to move closer to the divine. The people of our state show their piety and devotion through victory on the battlefield.
policies.name: Faith and Power

desc: Faith is the unifying power which keeps the state and the people together. The government exists for the sole purpose of ensuring that this unity remains unbroken.
policies.name: Belief and Unity

desc: The faith and the state are the two pillars that hold up the world. Our laws are holy, and they cannot be questioned.
policies.name: Church and State

desc: The only relationship that matters is that between lowly mortals and the immortal divine. Our state exists merely to remind people of the proper ways to devote themselves to their faith.
policies.name: God and Man

desc: We are a highly organized state oriented around a faith that is itself highly disorganized. By enacting an official hierarchy for our religion, we may convert more followers to the true faith.
policies.name: Organize Our Faith

desc: Religion is the pillar of our entire society, and as such, the nature of our faith plays a role in all facets of our culture. No major decisions can be made without carefully considering the religious perspective of taking these actions.
entities.name: Nature of our Faith

desc: There can only be one nature of Jesus.
policies.name: Single Nature

desc: The two natures of Jesus are combined into a single one (''μια φύσις'').
policies.name: Composite Nature

desc: The aspect of Jesus contains a dual nature, both human and divine (''Δυοφυσιτισμός'').
policies.name: Dual Nature

desc: While hosting two natures, divinity and humanity, these two aspects of Jesus are completely separate.
policies.name: Separate Nature

desc: Known also as physis (''φύσις''), this tenet rests at the core of our beliefs. It stands for the undisputed fact that Jesus Christ is of a dual and harmonious nature. The coexistence of humanity and divinity is the basis of coexistence that we shall strive to live by.
entities.name: Nature

desc: Only an aggressive attitude will keep us safe. We will use whatever tools we have to make it clear that whoever attacks us will pay a high cost.
policies.name: Belligerent Stance

desc: The time of fighting is over, and we must pivot towards employing more diplomacy. After all 'you catch more flies with honey than with vinegar'`.
policies.name: Conciliatory Stance

desc: Our lands are rugged as our people. Let our enemies come and bleed in our soil; future harvests will grow stronger.
policies.name: Defensive Stance

desc: We fear nobody, and as the old saying goes 'the best defense is a good offense'. We will attack first, and be deadlier than those who threaten our existence!
policies.name: Offensive Stance

desc: Being positioned between two larger nations has forced our nation to adapt or die. With a mixture of intelligent alliances and swift military actions, our realm has managed to survive despite its smaller size. This ability to quickly adjust our actions to suit our specific needs is an edge that we should never lose.
entities.name: Navarrese Adaptability

desc: Our naval influence shall be felt without the expense of our fleet leaving port except under the most favorable of conditions.
policies.name: Fleet in Being

desc: We shall reject the nation of forcing slaves and condemned men to row our galleys. Free men, resilient in the face of adversity and resistant to defection, shall be the muscle of our navy.
policies.name: Free Oarsmen
