desc: Our fleet's prime directive is to serve the financial interests of the state. Every effort shall be made to ensure our cargo ships are always laden with foreign riches.
policies.name: Merchant Navy

desc: With established Prize Law and generous Letters of Marque, we will nurture a custom of seizing enemy ships intact.
policies.name: Ship Boarding

desc: In a world of rapid change, the seas remain crucially important to our nation. Both as a means to secure our dominance and as the first line of defense, our 'wooden wall' of warships shall prevail.
policies.name: Wooden Wall

desc: A grand convoy shall accompany the treasure fleets that bring the wealth of our foreign possessions into our home ports.
policies.name: Grand Armada

desc: To establish a truly global empire, we must be skilled at launching assaults on enemy forts from the sea.
policies.name: Portuguese Marines

desc: The Mediterranean has many naval powers, yet none of them possess either our experience or our legislative expertise. The Ordinances of our fleet ensure that our navy is always prepared for any kind of engagement on the sea.
policies.name: Ordinance of the Sea

desc: Others brag about their superior ship designs, or their foothardy sailors who fight until they reach a pointless death. We, however, know better. No fleet, regardless of its construction quality or the mettle of the men it carries, can achieve victory without a strong leader. We shall embrace this philosophy and thereby vastly improve our naval efficacy.
policies.name: Danish Admiralty

desc: Ever since the very foundation of our nation, our people have lived off the ocean and the coast. Fishing, raiding, sea battles - our sailors have more experience than those of any other maritime nation, and we shall promote this expertise even further.
policies.name: Norwegian Sailors

desc: Galleys form the backbone of our national and commercial security. As such, a great focus of our naval and military tactics revolve around how to use our finest galleys to best any kind of naval foe.
policies.name: Venetian Galleys

desc: Our great navy is in dire need of sailors. Conscripting oarsmen and chaining them securely to our ships will ensure we have plenty of seamen to staff our new fleet... whether they like it or not.
policies.name: Venetian Oarsmen Conscription

desc: The nations of Europe use their navies to project their power through warfare on the sea. We, on the other hand, shall use our navy to reach the furthest corners of the world, so we can trade with foreign cultures while our neighbors bombard each other's coasts.
policies.name: Dutch Trade Fleet

desc: Our people have pursued whales to the very end of the world, raided coasts, and brought back precious goods from other lands, learning the secrets of the ocean over many years of exploration. These experiences have made our sailors courageous and reliable, a valuable addition to any navy that employs them.
policies.name: Basque Mariners

desc: Naval Doctrines represent skillsets in which our [
] can specialize. The longer we work at doctrines, the more entrenched they become in our navies and the better we get at them. Over time this can lead to powerful bonuses for our glorious fleets.
entities.name: Naval Doctrine

desc: The Nobility class has served our state well for generations. As it grows, it is only fitting that we continue to confer great privileges to those families who are devoted to our cause.
policies.name: Strengthen Rights of the Nobility

desc: As the state grows, it is becoming apparent that the old noble families have too much influence and power. Their jealous concern over these ancient privileges greatly hinders the development of our government.
policies.name: Curtail the Nobility

desc: The aristocratic class is not an enemy to the government, but an extension of the central power. Giving them the right to rule over the rural areas, while separating from national concerns, ensures a distinct separation of roles in the government.
policies.name: Rural Noble Authority

desc: It is becoming quite difficult to keep the Nobility loyal to the Crown. Establishing an electoral system will guarantee their allegiance, and has the additional bonus of ensuring a safe succession.
policies.name: Nobility Electorate

desc: Lei Mental defines the royal territories as inalienable. As such, land grants made by the monarch cannot be subdivided, and only eldest sons can inherit territories granted to members of the Nobility.
policies.name: Lei Mental

desc: A compilation of the laws of the realm, made to please the different estates of our realm, especially the nobles, as it sets 'mayorazgo', the entail of a family group, as the main inheritance system.

mods.label: Possible Nobles in Towns and Cities

policies.name: Leyes de Toro

desc: The position of the Nobility is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Nobility

desc: It is no mere coincidence that the Silk Road has been the source of much prosperity for the Middle Kingdom, for it is through trade and foreign exchange that a nation benefits.
policies.name: Allow Trade

desc: The seas and oceans bring trouble. Piracy, smuggling... sometimes even would-be usurpers hide themselves behind waves and tides. And yet, maritime trade also brings fortune and discovery. In order to let wealth and innovations flow freely into our great realm, we should establish Seaban regulations.
policies.name: Hǎijìn

desc: The Middle Kingdom has been expanding its power outwards since its inception, but external threats mean we require a certain degree of caution about who is able to enter its borders.
entities.name: Outwards View

desc: The state and the Patriarchy are two entirely separate entities which do not meddle in each other's affairs.
policies.name: Separated Patriarchy

desc: The Patriarchy assumes an influential position in the state and possesses authority over the religious matters of the country.
policies.name: State Patriarchy

desc: The head of the state is also the head of the Patriarchy. Religious matters are handled as if they were typical government issues.
policies.name: Combined Patriarchy

desc: While the Church has played a major role in the history of the state, it is becoming apparent that its position within our country needs to be rethought. By establishing the Most Holy Synod, the ruler keeps the influence of the Patriarchy in check.
policies.name: The Most Holy Synod

desc: The Patriarchate is a major pillar of our faith, and an institution with considerable influence over the state.
entities.name: Role of the Patriarchate

desc: Where other classes derive their power from material wealth and land ownership, the strength of the Commoners comes from their sheer quantity. They outnumber other estate greatly, and once organized, could pose a serious threat to our national stability. Safeguarding and strengthening the rights of the working class will reduce the chance that they will revolt.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Common Language

policies.name: Strengthen Rights of the Commoners

desc: The teeming population of our underclass poses a perpetual threat to the stability and survival of our state. Without a strong and persuasive ruler to keep them in check, the state could fall into anarchy. We cannot allow them to have a taste of the rights and privileges afforded to their betters, which could seduce them into rebellion.

mods.label: Prefers Court Language to be Common Language

policies.name: Curtail the Commoners

desc: The position of the Commoners is not only reinforced by their privileges, but also by our laws.
entities.name: Rights of the Commoners

desc: The Hre and other representatives will travel to different cities across the Holy Roman Empire, convening Diets where and when needed rather on a regular schedule or in a set location.
policies.name: Traveling Diet

desc: Previously, Imperial Diets convened irregularly in various cities across the Holy Roman Empire, requiring the Hre and other representatives to travel each time. By establishing a permanent, continuously-sitting Diet, we shall create a standing assembly that operates on a system of constant deliberation, rather than sporadic meetings.
policies.name: Perpetual Diet

desc: Previously, Imperial Diets convened irregularly in various cities across the Holy Roman Empire, requiring the Hre and other representatives to travel each time. By establishing a permanent, continuously-sitting Diet, we shall create a standing assembly that operates on a system of constant deliberation, rather than sporadic meetings.
entities.name: Perpetual Diet

desc: The nature of Christ and God is one but the same.
policies.name: Single Hypostasis

desc: Christ and God are different manifestations of the divine essence.
policies.name: Multiple Hypostases

desc: Deriving from the core concept of concrete reality (''υπόστασις''), this tenet delves into the essence and nature of Christ and God, and their divine essences taking a single or multiple manifestations.
entities.name: Hypostasis

desc: Our nation fully embraces acts of piracy against our enemies. Our reputation may suffer for using these tactics, but the economic benefits can be enormous.

mods.label: Can be Target of Anti-Piracy War Casus Belli

policies.name: State Piracy

desc: While piracy is not something we necessarily support, it does present a marvelous opportunity to pit career criminals against our enemies. We will issue Letters of Marque to privateer captains so they can freely attack our enemies' ships without fear of prosecution.
policies.name: Letters of Marque

desc: Our nation is devoted to eradicting any pirate threats that may arise. Any act of piracy will be punished and prosecuted, and ships conducting these illicit acts will be attacked without mercy.

mods.label: Can Create Anti-Piracy War Casus Belli

policies.name: Anti-Piracy

desc: By granting several letters of marque to anyone wishing to serve us, we can expand our navy without needing to construct any new vessels.
policies.name: Sea Beggars

desc: Piracy laws define the official position our nation adopts when addressing the challenges posed by piracy. These laws encompass statutes, regulations, and legal doctrines aimed at combating or managing piracy effectively. They embody the collective strategy and measures our nation implements to uphold maritime security and protect our waters from piracy threats. Or perhaps they are just the rules we stick to when committing acts of piracy...
entities.name: Piracy Law

desc: Establishing the Estudo Geral within the periphery of the court will allow us to centralize power and to exercise greater control over the University's operations.
policies.name: Estudo Geral in Lisbon

desc: By situating the national University in the famously scholarly settlement of Coimbra, we will safeguard its independence and assure the estates of our educational goals.
policies.name: Estudo Geral in Coimbra

desc: The Por Estudo Geral is a national University that aims to educate the citizens of our humble state. Its location and proximity to the capital is a crucial matter to us.
entities.name: Estudo Geral

desc: The Hre is no longer a monarch with power within the Holy Roman Empire. All laws and policies are now in the hands of the Imperial Diet and the Prince-Elector.
policies.name: Holy Roman Figurehead

desc: The power held by the Hre is carefully balanced: strong enough to protect and reform the Holy Roman Empire, yet not so overwhelming as to threaten our Prince-Elector or member states.
policies.name: Kaisertum

desc: The authority of the Hre is vastly expanded, allowing them to enforce policies in the Imperial Diet for the betterment of the Holy Roman Empire.
policies.name: Improved Imperial Authority

desc: The many liberties and privileges granted to the Imperial Princes are hereby abolished. The Hre shall centralize authority, turning the Holy Roman Empire into a unified entity under singular rule.
policies.name: Revoke Privilegia

desc: Decentralization in the Holy Roman Empire is no more. The entire Empire shall be united into a single nation-state, which will shape the fate of the world itself!
policies.name: Renovatio Imperii

desc: The Power of the Hre is a complicated topic. Members of the Holy Roman Empire and Prince-Elector alike have conflicting interests with those of the Hre, yet they recognize that a powerless  Hre is in no position to protect the Empire.
entities.name: Power of the [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('hre').GetLeaderTitle]

desc: We will enforce strict prohibition on the export of our precious Gold and Silver reserves to foreign lands. This preserves our wealth for domestic use, shielding our treasures from the greedy eyes of other nations. While this measure may safeguard our riches, it comes at the cost of international trade opportunities. A solemn decision for those who prioritize the sanctity of our vaults over global commerce...
policies.name: Export Ban

desc: The trade of our valuable Gold and Silver resources is managed with a watchful eye. This balanced approach limits the quantity of these precious metals that can be traded, ensuring that our wealth remains largely within our borders. By doing so, we strike a compromise between bolstering our economy and protecting our national riches. A prudent choice for rulers who seek both financial stability and regional influence.
policies.name: Regulated Export

desc: We shall open the floodgates and allow unrestricted trade of our Gold and Silver reserves with foreign nations. With this bold step, we embrace the potential for unparalleled wealth accumulation through international commerce. However, this policy exposes our treasures to the risk of being dispersed across the world, making them vulnerable to the greed of rival powers. A daring option for rulers who seek to dominate the global market and reap the rewards of boundless riches.
policies.name: Unlimited Export

desc: Goods Gold and Silver are the materials necessary for the minting of coins. As our state is in the highly enviable position to gather these precious metals ourselves, it is our right to decide who gains access to these resources.
entities.name: Precious Metal Distribution

desc: Only the State has the right to print the news. All other forms of press are illegal.
policies.name: State Press Only

desc: All printing must be approved by the state, which has the inalienable legal right to censor any material it opposes.
policies.name: Censored Press

desc: Citizens can print whatever they like without interference or sanction.
policies.name: Free Press

desc: This determines how print media outlets in a country are run and regulated.
entities.name: Press Laws

desc: As a Republic, the guiding principles of our state must be those that further the efficiency of our political apparatus and ideals.
policies.name: Political Principle

desc: One of the primary functions of the state is to uphold proper  moral values. As our Republic in many ways relies on the virtuous behavior of its citizens, corruption and sin must be exposed and rooted out for the good of the entire country.
policies.name: Moral Principle

desc: The highest principle of our republic is the protection of its people. Although not a popular topic in our government, it is important to maintain a military force for self-defense and maintenance of internal stability.
policies.name: Protection Principle

desc: Our Republic is surrounded by enemies who seek to destroy us utterly. It is our uttermost priority - our principle - to use our military might to expand our borders.
policies.name: Military Principle

desc: The Enlightenment is the next intellectual and philosophical step for our society. Embracing the ideas of the Enlightenment is crucial if we wish to progress into a new era.
policies.name: Enlightened Principle

desc: Our Republic is based on the principle of commercialism. Human nature is the driving factor behind the necessity of trade, capital, and business as our Burghers pursue profit.
policies.name: Commercialist Principle

desc: If we wish to be an example for all our citizens, the Republic must uphold principles which dictate the course of action we take with our policies.
entities.name: Administrative Principles

desc: Christ has two persons, divine and human.
policies.name: Dyoprosopic Concept

desc: Originally meaning Mask (''πρόσωπον''), this tenet centers on the Person of Christ, and whether He is a single individual or includes two different divine and human individuals.
entities.name: Prosopon

desc: Provincial governors only spread corruption and laziness. We must keep them on a short leash so that the authority of the central government is not diluted even in the most faraway regions.
policies.name: Curtailed Governors

desc: The position of provincial governor is prestigious, and very much in demand. Established governors with clearly assigned territory and administration duties will allow the cogs of our government to turn more smoothly.
policies.name: Established Provincial Governors

desc: The territory of the Middle Kingdom is too vast for simple governors to handle. Let us establish the position of the Zǒngdū, a viceroy overseeing more than one province. They will be directing the provincial affairs as the Middle Kingdom's representative so that the less crucial matters do not have to be reported to the capital.
policies.name: Zǒngdū

desc: The native Chieftains in remote prefectures, also known as Tǔsī, are hereditary rulers of local minorities. These leaders might seem useful now and then due to their ties with the locals, but they have frequently proven to be a long-term risk to regional stability. By slowly replacing them with officials appointed by the central government, maintaining tranquillity on a regional level will become easier.
policies.name: The Gǎitǔguīliú System

desc: To manage the numerous subjects and lesser states from outlying regions within and beyond the Imperial border, the Ministry of Rites is now deemed to be insufficient and inappropriate. We shall establish an office that focuses on dealing with them.
policies.name: Lǐfān Yuàn

desc: The vastness of the Middle Kingdom is unparalleled. In order to effectively rule our massive holdings, we shall establish a system of provincial administrators.
entities.name: Provincial Governorship

desc: Our current levies are insufficient to handle the current level of conflict we must endure. Expanding the size of our levies and the number of soldiers on the battlefield will surely bring us to victory, albeit to the potential detriment of our general population.
policies.name: Expanded Levies

desc: Our population is precious, and the Nobles of our country are willing to lay down their lives to protect our lands. Although their blood is worth more than those they protect, with that heritage comes greater skill on the battlefield.
policies.name: A Noble Army

desc: Every vessel in our nation should be mobilized in case of war. Therefore, the state must maintain a detailed overview of all our ships, including merchant vessels, in case we need them.
policies.name: Regulated Naval Service

desc: The ''Calpulli'' are housing units, similar to neighborhoods, where Commoners live together in a kin-based system. This system not only helps create more national stability, but also gives us a reliable source of manpower for our constant state of warfare.
policies.name: Calpulli

desc: In steppe tradition, one-fifth of the spoils of war went to the chieftain. Therefore, now one-fifth of all slaves taken in war will go to the state.
policies.name: Pençik Tax

desc: Our forefathers favored exemplary defense. They withstood the test of time and foe alike. It is now our turn to go on the offensive and stage a show of strength against our heretic and heathen neighbors alike, through the use of a reformed and aggressive military force.
policies.name: Reformed Hussite Tactics

desc: Though we can call our levies in times of need, it is better to let the mercenaries lead the charge into the fray. At best, their expertise will bring us victory, and at worst, their bodies will protect our fighters during the battle.
policies.name: Mercenary Army

desc: Standing armies are the exception rather than the norm. As such, our state must rely on mercenaries to be our state's fighting forces, which means that better offers from other powers could led them to abandon our service. Thanks to expanded ''Condottieri'' contracts, we can ensure these professional soldiers stay loyal to the state.
policies.name: Condottieri Contracts

desc: Slaves are acquired for the ruling household through the practice of ''devşirme'': Carefully chosen non-Muslim children, usually Christians between the ages of 12 and 14, are sent to live with Turkish families to learn their language and the rules of Islam beliefs before eventually being brought to the capital. Most join the Janissaries, a highly disciplined standing army, while those who displayed particular leadership and intellectual skilled are enrolled directly into the royal household as pages.
policies.name: Devşirme System

desc: Regardless of aristocratic objections, the Black Army is undeniably an effective military force. We shall institutionalize their company, and ensure that there is always a reserve of veteran soldiers waiting to join their ranks.
policies.name: Black Army

desc: We have had no need of a standing army for centuries, as levies and mercenaries have so far been the ones to fight our battles. However, times have changed, and the scale of war has far exceeded what untrained soldiers can handle. It is therefore now time to establish a standing army.
policies.name: Early Standing Army

desc: We have had no need of a standing army for centuries, as levies and mercenaries have so far been the ones to fight our battles. However, times have changed, and the scale of war has far exceeded what untrained soldiers can handle. It is therefore now time to establish a standing army.
policies.name: New Model Army

desc: The Allotment System, or ''Indelningsverket'', is a military conscription system that enables quick mobilization. Every tenth man in the country between the ages of fifteen and forty-four will be permanently conscripted into the national infantry, while the Nobility, while exempt from taxes, must provide cavalry.
policies.name: Allotment System

desc: The Canton System will divide the country into adminstrative districts called ''cantons'', each responsible for army recruitment and linking the local population closely to the government. This system relies on voluntary enrollment rather than coercive recruiting. However, each canton must provide a minimum number of soldiers.
policies.name: Canton System

desc: Instead of relying on entrenched nobles to serve within our army, we could grant everyone an opportunity to serve within every rank of the army, as long as they prove they can fulfill that role.
policies.name: Manṣabdār Organization

desc: Although today's armies perpetually grow in size, the acumen and morale of these ragtag recuits is not nearly as grand. Our men, on the other hand, are fewer in number, but make up for it with the kind of iron discipline that can turn the tide of battle.
policies.name: Elite Training

desc: We have, up to now, been very selective about who can serve as an enlisted member of our military. We only took the poorest and most desperate — basically, the people no one else would miss. Now, though, we shall open up the ranks to everyone who wishes to serve and has no significant wealth to speak of.
policies.name: Mass Army Policy

desc: Soldiers split their time between family life on rural military-run farms, and in direct service to the army. Their families are primed to provide future contributions to the military, ensuring we have a continous supply of new recruits while simultaneously working the land.
policies.name: Military Settlements

desc: Piracy is an attractive prospect for privateers. The promise of treasure, fame, and more rum for their bellies leads many brave sailors into a life full of adventure — and danger...
policies.name: Benefits for Privateers

desc: Green Standard Army is an auxiliary army comprised of Hàn Chinese nationals that serves to bolster our forces as well as to police our conquests in East Asia.
policies.name: Green Standard Army

desc: The Varangian Guard, drawn from Norse, English, and other northern peoples, bound by personal oath to the Emperor serve as the imperial bodyguard and household shock troops. Their loyalty is purchased, not inherited, making them immune to the factional intrigues that plague Greek noble officers. Their axes have defended the throne for generations, and their fierce discipline sets a standard for the whole army.
policies.name: Varangian Guard

desc: Through the sweeping reforms born of crisis, the Tágmata have been reforged into something closer to the fearsome professional soldiers of old. Stricter drill, restored imperial funding, and a renewed sense of purpose have elevated the regiments above the diminished force they had become. These soldiers stand apart from the feudal levy not merely in name but in discipline, cohesion, and battlefield effectiveness.
policies.name: Reformed Tágmata

desc: Battles cannot be won with no soldiers on the field! Recruiting fighters is an absolute necessity. As time goes on, how we recruit soldiers may change, and our forces will adapt to it as needed.
entities.name: Recruitment Law

desc: The terms our officials currently serve are too short for them to fully realize larger and more complicated projects. This has the effects of feeding populist sentiment, and often leads to short-sighted, less effective policy development. Let us reform our election system to allow for longer terms so that our elected officials have the time they need to properly conduct their office.
policies.name: Consolidated Power

desc: Serving long terms makes rulers reckless, and is contrary to the very idea of a republic. Let us reform our election system to set shorter term limits, thereby ensuring better accountability from our elected officials.
policies.name: Frequent Elections

desc: Elections are the cornerstone of our republic, ensuring that there are reasonable limits on those in power while giving the people the ability to select rulers that best serve their interests.
entities.name: Election

desc: The landholders are the heart of power in any society, and ours is no exception. Let us extend the power to vote to all who hold land, and weight their electoral power in accordance with the size of their properties.
policies.name: Landholders

desc: A republic relies on its citizens to function, and so it is only right that each of our citizens holds the power to vote for who will lead the country. Attaining the privilege of citizenship will also be an incentive for our citizens to be on their best behavior.
policies.name: Citizenry

desc:
Connections are more powerful than any sword could ever be. Through the installment of a dynasty as the political head of the state, we can build diplomatic relations with monarchies while still maintaining the principles of the republic.
That the elected ruler seems to be a member of the same family is just a pure coincidence.
policies.name: Dynastic Rule

desc: The Board of Admiralty is the highest maritime office of the state. Led by the Lord High Admiral, the board ensures the military and commercial professionalism of our navy.
policies.name: Board of Admiralty

desc: The republic is a thorn in the side of many potential enemies who seek to destroy us. For the sake of the country's safety, we granted the generals the reins of our government. May their experience and love for their home country protect the republic.
policies.name: Military Rulership

desc: Elections are the foundational concept of our republic, and as such, the most important factor in determining the course of the Republic is deciding who is eligible vote in those elections.
entities.name: Republican Electorate Law

desc: This nation will is a guardian of Republican ideals, such as rule through elected representatives, civic virtue, and constitutional limits on power. Citizens actively participate in their governance through voting and holding office.
policies.name: Republicanism

desc: While it is not a monarchy, this form of republic concentrates power in the hands of a small ruling group that is not accountable to citizens. Dissent is not tolerated. Despite being a republic, administrations in these countries are more concerned with maintaining their own power than they are with the rights of their citizens.
policies.name: Authoritarianism

desc: Over time, several families have emerged as prominent leaders, frequently seeking and assuming roles in the government. At this point, it is expected of them to shoulder the burden of leadership, just as it is expected for the state to offer these responsibilities to their scions.
policies.name: Political Dynasties

desc: Our republic does not elect its rulers based on connections or influence from the oligarchs. Instead, the masses of our country vote according to what skills the candidate offers. This system of meritocracy does not differentiate between genders, and is present in all aspects of our society.
policies.name: Meritocratic Rule

desc: Politeia balances the interests of both wealthy and common citizens through participation in government. This system creates stability through compromise, protecting the interests of both sides and ensuring that neither faction can dominate.
policies.name: Virtues of Politeia

desc: Religious values inform political life in our republic, shaping both civic and governmental culture. Religious institutions play important advisory roles in public affairs, citizens are encouraged to consider religious ethics when voting, and leaders are expected to govern in accordance with moral teachings.
policies.name: Religious Values

desc: Our Republic is founded on the principle that power should be in the hands of the people, not a single absolutist ruler. Yet as with any government, its laws and decisions must be respected and obeyed to maintain order, necessitating the creation of complex administrations in order to govern.
entities.name: Foundation of Republic

desc: As our country grows, so does our need to be able to take swift actions. The only way to ensure this is by broadening the powers of the executive branch so that it can do whatever it needs without hindrance.
policies.name: Broad Executive Power

desc: No single person can rule a country as complex as ours. Concentrating such power in the hands of one ruler also runs contrary to the Republican ideals of our ancestors. Transferring some of our authority and responsibilities to local governments, which maintaining an ultimate centralized authority, is how we can best meet the needs of our ever-growing state.
policies.name: Devolution Of Powers

desc: While some of our elected officials represent the people of their constituencies, we must never forget that it is the President who ultimately represents all our people. The role of our elected representatives should be merely to advise the President, who wields absolute power over the Republic.
policies.name: Absolute Power of the President

desc: Those who hold on to power for too long cannot be trusted. Our Republic will now focus on electing new officials, ones whose hands are clean of corruption and shady business.
policies.name: New Men

desc: As any government, the Republic must not only make decisions, but also act upon them. To do so, it needs a way of exercising its executive capabilities so that they reach even the furthest areas of the country.
entities.name: Republican Power

desc: The Nobility are an integral part of our government. In order to better control, reward, and gain support from these ancient aristocratic families, the Nobility are tied closely to the monarch and the royal court.
policies.name: Aristocratic Court

desc: The royal court serves as the center of the state and culture. Administrative, diplomatic, and military actions are just as much of a focus of the court as the cultural and internal politics of the state are.
policies.name: Balanced Court

desc: The court is first and foremost the household of the royal family, and serves as a center of culture and prestige. Governmental and administrative affairs are separated from court life.
policies.name: Court of Culture

desc: To better manage the sheer size of our nation, the royal court is not bound to a single location. Instead, it migrates throughout the land and manages local administration on site.
policies.name: Itinerant Court

desc: Much of our court life is secluded and gender-segregated, centered around a harem where enslaved servants and concubines vie for influence over the ruler.
policies.name: Royal Harem

desc: Spending money on anything for the court beyond absolute necessities is a ridiculous notion that will only encourage complacency and laziness. The monarch will live a frugal live, and dedicate more of the budget towards the army.
policies.name: Military Court

desc: Our court and our ruler must strive towards humanist ideals. We must become a prime destination for aspiring artists and philosophers.
policies.name: Humanist Court

desc: While warfare is the lifeblood of the state, music, art, and poetry are equally essential to the greatness of our country. Cultural traditions from the lands we have subdued will no longer be considered alien, but be used to develop our cultural enlightenment.
policies.name: Timurid Court

desc: 'Paradise lies at the feet of your mother', and as such, the queen mother should hold the highest position at court, have the right to oversee council meetings, and through her wisdom and benevolence, play an important role in most affairs of the state.
policies.name: Valide Sultan

desc: Instead of depending on our own culture, we can take inspiration from other courts in order to further strenghthen our owm.
policies.name: Foreign Customs

desc: An emperor born in the sacred Purple Chamber of the Great Palace carries an aura of legitimacy unmatched by any rival. Our court ceremony, codified in the ''De Ceremoniis'', projects the majesty of a living Roman Empire to every envoy who enters our capital. The elaborate protocol is costly, but the prestige it radiates solidifies the dynasty's claim before the world.
policies.name: Porphyrogénitus Court

desc: The traditions and the culture of the court play a significant role in the stability of the Monarchy. These customs will ensure the safe transition of power from ruler to heir, and limit the court intrigues significantly.
entities.name: Royal Court Customs

desc: The earthly rulers are the main guardians and guarantors of the Church, and as such their decisions affect how the Patriarch operates. They are the representatives of God, to rule His kingdom here on Earth.
policies.name: Caesaropapism

desc: Render unto Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and unto God the things that are God's.
policies.name: Independent Authorities

desc: The Patriarch works for the souls of the people and that sometimes puts him in interaction with the earthly authority. What role should the countries rulers take when interacting with the Patriarch is also a matter of the faith.
entities.name: Ruler and Patriarch Relations

desc: The Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation shall be chosen every 2 years.
policies.name: Biyearly Elections

desc: The Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation shall be chosen every 4 years.
policies.name: 4-yearly Elections

desc: The Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation shall be chosen every 8 years.
policies.name: 8-yearly Elections

desc: As the matters of the Ruling Period are cleared, a new topic arises which handles the frequency of the elections of a new Swiss Confederation.
entities.name: Election Frequency

desc: The Swiss Confederation is directly elected by the members of the Swiss Confederation. Every member has a singular vote, and every member shall be eligible to represent the Confederation.
policies.name: Direct Vote

desc: Only the Lord can decide who shall represent the Swiss Confederation. The election process is handled via a secret lottery process with fate as the conclusive factor.
policies.name: Lottery

desc: The Swiss Confederation is decided by turns. Every member of the Swiss Confederation shall represent the confederation at least once before a former leader can take over the mantle once again.
policies.name: Rotation

desc: The process of electing the Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation is a delicate matter which requires an exact legislature to be handled properly.
entities.name: Election Method

desc: We cannot allow petty disputes to escalate into bloody conflicts. Every member of the Swiss Confederation shall state their issue with another member in front of the judges of the Confederation instead of on the battlefield.
policies.name: Forbid Internal Wars

desc: Although generally not desirable, conflict is part of human nature, and it is through it that we get to grow stronger.
policies.name: Allow Internal Wars

desc: While the Swiss Confederation is first and foremost a union for defensive purposes, it is clear that the internal affairs of the Confederation must be handled too.
entities.name: Internal Politics

desc: The confederation is a Swiss organization, and as such only those who are of its culture and geography are allowed to join.
policies.name: Native Swiss Only

desc: The influence of the Swiss people is growing far beyond the historical area of the Swiss Confederation. Geographical limitations are no longer adequate, and as such the law needs reconsideration.
policies.name: Swiss Culture

desc: The influence and power of the Swiss Confederation is projected not only by the Swiss people, but also those which we consider close relatives to our culture.
policies.name: Relatives of the Swiss

desc: The Swiss Confederation is an organization originally made by the Swiss people to defend themselves against the growing influence of the Habsburg in the local region. However, the rules who can join are never set in stone...
entities.name: Membership Regulation

desc: Adjustment of laws and policies is a frequent act, and as such happens in Swiss Confederation on a base of every 4 years.
policies.name: Frequent Policy Proposals

desc: While a significant process, administrating the laws and policy proposals within the Swiss Confederation takes considerable effort, which allows law proposals only every 8 years.
policies.name: Moderate Policy Proposals

desc: A law regulating the administration of law proposals within the Swiss Confederation.
entities.name: Policy Proposal Frequency

desc: The Swiss Confederation has the right to request aid from the members of the Swiss Confederation which can range from financial to military support.
policies.name: Representative Power

desc: The power of the Swiss Confederation is limited with the exception in the matters of religious affairs of the Swiss Confederation.
policies.name: Religious Power

desc: The leading Swiss Confederation rules over the Swiss Confederation as if it was a singular state. As such, they enjoy all the privileges and duties as if they were a monarch of the Confederation.
policies.name: Absolute Power

desc: The representative of the Confederation could request for more power and influence within the union in order to strengthen their position on the public stage.
entities.name: [GetUniqueInternationalOrganization('swiss_confederation').GetLeaderTitle] Power

desc: While the Swiss Confederation is a capable network of alliance defending its members from foreign powers, it is ill-suited to withstand the military might of far greater states. Remaining in the Holy Roman Empire will provide the Swiss with more, much-needed support.
policies.name: Remain in the Empire

desc: Although external enemies are not uncommon, the biggest threats the Swiss Confederation faces come from within the Holy Roman Empire itself, which originally promised to defend its members. Staying within the Empire only jeopardizes our own survivability.
policies.name: Leave the Empire

desc: The Swiss Confederation has been part of the Holy Roman Empire since its inception. However, the The Reformation left a bitter taste for many members of the Confederation...
entities.name: Imperial Relations

desc: The stability and safety of the Swiss Confederation is above the religious quarrels of the The Reformation. Every member shall withdraw hostile relations with members of a different faith.
policies.name: Mending the Schism

desc: Religion plays a significant role in the lives of its members and as such the religious unity of the Swiss Confederation is of great priority. All cantons shall follow the same faith one way or another.
policies.name: Enforce Religious Unity

desc: With the breakout of the The Reformation, the religious unity of the Confederation is a precarious situation. A solution must be found or else the conflict of faith threatens to tear the union apart.
entities.name: Religious Affairs

desc: Some Cantons happen to be richer and more influential than others. As such, the Swiss Confederation shall be represented not by a man but by a city-state.
policies.name: Canton Representative

desc: The Cantons of the Swiss Confederation shall give up a bit of their influence to enact a single man to become the face of the Confederation.
policies.name: Councillor Representative

desc: Every kind of organization will require a spokesman - a representative - who shall be the face to the political entities inside and outside of the organization. The Swiss Confederation might pose an exception to this rule though...
entities.name: Swiss Representative

desc: The Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation is only in charge for a set period of time. Afterwards, their term ends and a new Swiss Confederation shall be elected.
policies.name: Timed

desc: The Swiss Confederation of the Swiss Confederation serves for their entire life. Only upon their death or expulsion, an election shall be held.
policies.name: Lifelong

desc: The Confederation might have a Swiss Confederation representing it. Yet, it must be determined if said Swiss Confederation shall serve the union lifelong or until a certain time has passed.
entities.name: Ruling Period

desc: The principles and methods of the Swiss Confederation are well received as every Canton enjoys having their voices heard. Yet, the decentralized nature of the confederation will always endanger the safety and security of the Swiss people. It is time to unify the Confederation into a singular state while maintaining the Republic.
policies.name: Found the Swiss Republic

desc: While it started as a republican union, the challenges the Swiss Confederation had to face have proven the superiority of a strong rule under a single Councillor. The future of the Swiss people can only be ensured under the authority of a proper Monarchy which shall replace the old Confederation.
policies.name: Found the Swiss Monarchy

desc: Neither the free will of the Republican votes nor the authoritarian power of a Monarchy has led the Swiss Confederation to the position it is now, but the will of the divine. Only as a unified Theocracy can the Swiss people prosper in this world.
policies.name: Found the Swiss Theocracy

desc: The Swiss lands have been splintered for far too long. If the people of the Alps wish to see prosperity and security, they have to unite under a single banner.
entities.name: Swiss Unification

desc: Members of the Swiss Confederation are only called to arms in a defensive war against external threats.
policies.name: Defensive Pact

desc: Members of the Swiss Confederation may call each other to their side in their own expansion attempts. In case of an external invasion, all members are called to arms to defend their fellow comrades of the Confederation.
policies.name: Swiss Alliance

desc: The Swiss Confederation is similar to a singular political entity to all external states. Each war - be it offensive or defensive in nature - shall call the military of all the members of the Confederation.
policies.name: United War Efforts

desc: The external threats of the Swiss Confederation are many. Unified terms of how the Swiss defend each other are needed if the Confederation is to survive the political anarchy around it.
entities.name: War Politics

desc: Roman and Curia influence have largely been curtailed in favor of the established government having direct jurisdiction of the religious institutions within Scotland.
policies.name: Government Jurisdiction

desc: While the government retains most influence over the religious institutions within Scotland, a special provision has been given to high ranking clergymen, allowing them to engage openly with the Curia.
policies.name: Limited Curia Access

desc: Scottish contribution to the Curia have become a burden on the state's finances. Seeking to curtail Curia contributions, the state has taken direct jurisdiction over the clergymen.
entities.name: Authority over the Clergy

desc: Holdings and titles are retained within a clan, only reverting back to the ruler when a clan lineage goes extinct.
policies.name: Direct Inheritance

desc: Newly established holdings and titles are assigned by the ruler's preference. Larger clans are typically favored as allies by the ruler and receive the lionshare of new titles.
policies.name: Distributed by the Ruler

desc: New holdings and titles default to the ruling dynasty, only rarely being given by them to other Scottish clans.
policies.name: Dynastic Holdings

desc: The inheritance of Scottish holdings is divided proportional to clan influence, with larger clans recieving more holdings. Clan holdings are passed directly to the heir, unless a title is revoked or goes extinct.
entities.name: Distribution of Scottish Clan Holdings

desc: Colonial ventures and attempts to establish trade companies in the new world have been deemed too great a risk to the financial stability of Scotland.
policies.name: No Colonial Ventures

desc: Colonial ventures have been deemed a worthwhile economic risk for the state, and have been officially sanctioned.
policies.name: Limited Colonial Ventures

desc: Through countless efforts by explorers and investors, Scotland has found its place in the sun amongst the colonial powers and reaps great benefits from its colonial possessions.
policies.name: Experienced Colonial Administration

desc: With tales of riches from the new world, Scotland stands to reap the benefits should it establish a sizable colonial basis. Although an overambition may prove catastrophic for the state's economic stability.
entities.name: Scottish Colonial Affairs

desc: Founded by the Buddhist monk Nichiren, most of its doctrine comes from the ''Lotus Sutra'', but opposes any form of deviation from mainstream teachings, including esoteric practices and rituals. It dictates that one's actions and their consequences, not only meditation, affect the achievement of enlightenment.
policies.name: Nichiren

desc: A school of Pure Land Buddhism, it was founded by Shinran, a monk originally from the Tendai school. He became disillusioned and went to study the traditions of Pure Land Buddhism, eventually founding a new branch. Focusing on ''Nenbutsu'', the recitation of the name of the Buddha, the expression ''Namu Amida Butsu'' has almost become synonymous with this school, used as a way of showing gratitude to the Buddha Amida.
policies.name: Jōdo Shinshū

desc: The oldest school of Tibetan Buddhism, it contains unique teachings not seen in any other form of Buddhism. It considers ''Dzogchen'', 'Great Perfection', the most direct path to enlightenment, prescribing this method above those advocated by other schools. However, it has been criticized by rival schools for lacking connection to later Indian tantric practices, as its texts derive from the first introduction of Buddhism into Tibet.
policies.name: Nyingma School

desc: Stressing compassion, study, and discipline, it attempts to create a comprehensive and systematic Mahāyāna Buddhist path to achieving enlightenment. It also has the objective of integrating laypeople into Buddhist daily life, while reserving tantric practices for advanced initiates.
policies.name: Kadam School

desc: The Kagyu School focuses on the ''Mahāmudrā'', the 'Great Seal', which is the symbol of attaining knowledge or awareness of the intrinsic emptiness of reality. Although the school itself has diverged into multiple sub-schools, all with their own small differences of interpretation and practices, all recognize the Mahāmudrā.
policies.name: Kagyu School

desc: Originating in the Sakya Monastery, it focuses on ''Lamdré'', a system of meditation with the maxim that the result of the practice is already intrinsically contained within the path. These teachings are contained in the tantra of ''Hevajra'', and the school contains multiple tantric practices.
policies.name: Sakya School

desc: The main practice of the Jonang School is the Kālacakra Tantra, and the school is a defender of the Shentong philosophy. In it, it holds that physical reality is empty of inherent existence, but in contrast ultimate reality — or Buddha-nature — is not. Buddha-nature is filled with its own innumerable awakened qualities.
policies.name: Jonang School

desc: The particular school of this sect, which may have some differences from mainstream of teachings.
entities.name: Sect School

desc: The Electorate of the Holy Roman Empire remains split between Prince-Elector and Archbishop-Elector.
policies.name: Traditional Electorate

desc: The previous positions of the Archbishop-Elector have been fully secularized.
policies.name: Secularized Electorate

desc: Traditionally the Electorate is split between the Prince-Elector and the Archbishop-Elector. In case political dynamics threaten the lands of the Archbishop-Elector, the empire might consider a full secularization of their positions.
entities.name: Secularization of the Electorate

desc: The Ḥanafī Madhhab is named after Abū Ḥanīfa Al-Nu'mān ibn Thābit. The school originated in Kufa and is prominent throughout the Farsi and Turkic world, including northern India. Though textual sources in the Qur'ān and Ḥadīth are given preference, Ḥanafī followers have an inclusive view of sources and also employ analogy (Qiyās), juristic discretion (Istiḥsan), and local customs ('Urf) in their jurisprudence. Some view it as the most flexible of the schools.
policies.name: Ḥanafī Jurisprudence

desc: The Ḥanbalī Madhhab is named after Aḥmad ibn Ḥanbal, and champions withholding from any speculative theology, Kalām. Ḥanbalī followers maintain that the Qur'ān and Sunnah are the only proper sources of jurisprudence and that they should be interpreted in a literal and traditionalist sense. Though it is accepted as a valid Madhhab, very few states actively promote the Ḥanbalī school, and it was banned by the Abbasid Caliphs.
policies.name: Ḥanbalī Jurisprudence

desc: The Mālikī Madhhab is named after Mālik ibn Anas and is prominent in particular throughout North Africa and Iberia. Jurisprudence is primarily based on the work and interpretations of ibn Anas and his student Saḥnūn as described in the al-Muwaṭṭa' and the Mudawwanah. One of the foremost centers of learning within the Mālikī School is the Great Mosque of Āl Qayrawān, near Tunis.
policies.name: Mālikī Jurisprudence

desc: The Shāfi'ī Madhhab is named after Imām Al-Shāfi'ī, and it is prominent in particular among Islam believers in Arabia, East Africa, and East Asia. Unlike other Madhhab, the Shāfi'ī reject Istiḥsan and Istislah as sources of Sharī'ah, instead only relying on what is textually in the Qur'ān or Ḥadīth.
policies.name: Shāfi'ī Jurisprudence

desc: The Ẓāhirī advocates for a strict adherence to the text of the Qur'ān, and focus on its external or apparent meaning. According to them, there can not be any conclusion drawn from reading the texts that is not in the texts themselves, otherwise Allāh would have explicitly expressed those already.
policies.name: Ẓāhirī Jurisprudence

desc: The Ismā'īlī Madhhab is named after Ismā'īl ibn Ja'far, the successor of Ja'far al-Ṣādiq, and was the dominant school of faith in the Fatimid Caliphate but has lost much ground since its fall. The Ismā'īlī school encompasses a number of increasingly divergent branches, and in many ways, they focus on the esoteric elements of Shiism faith more than the Ja'farī or Zaydī.
policies.name: Ismā'īlī Jurisprudence

desc: The Ja'farī Madhhab is named after Ja'far al-Ṣādiq, the sixth Imām, and it focuses on independent reasoning by experts of Islamic Law, prefering that over analogy when establishing the Law. It also allows for a temporary marriage lasting a predeterminate period of time.
policies.name: Ja'farī Jurisprudence

desc: Also called 'Fivers', the Zaydī current is named after Zayd ibn 'Alī, the grandson of Muḥammad's son 'Alī, and follows his teachings as described in the Majmu' al-Fiqh. Zaydī followers emphasize justice and human responsibility and descend from those who supported Zayd's original revolt against the Umayyad Caliph. Zaydī people entirely reject religious dissimulation as practiced by many Shiism followers, and it is the most similar to Sunnism.
policies.name: Zaydī Jurisprudence

desc: Believed to be a descendant of the Al-Khawārij, who first were supporters of 'Alī ibn Abī Ṭālib but later rejected his arbitration. The Ibāḍī school distanced itself from the Al-Khawārij following 'Abd Allāh ibn Ibāḍ, taking a more moderate approach and a more positive view towards different Muslim branches, having similarities with many of the other schools.
policies.name: Ibāḍī Jurisprudence

desc: Sharī'ah Law is a comprehensive and deeply entrenched legal system in Islamic countries that governs many aspects of life, from personal conduct to matters of state. It has provided stability and continuity for centuries, but its strict and sometimes harsh penalties can be controversial and divisive.
entities.name: Sharī'ah Jurisprudence

desc: The conduct of our religious and palatial affairs by the Lǐbù is a matter of utmost delicacy and importance. By ensuring a well-implemented and capable ministry dedicated to the preservation and display of rites, we will maintain an excellent standard.
policies.name: Ministry of Rites

desc: In charge of all the people that serve in our administration, the Lìbù is the cornerstone of our government. By keeping its offices running smoothly, we will ensure in turn that our government positions are well staffed.
policies.name: Ministry of Personnel

desc: The Hùbù is in charge of everything money and currency related, from establishing censuses to collecting taxes and administrating the currency values. As such, keeping the ministry in good function is crucial for the prosperity of our realm.
policies.name: Ministry of Revenue

desc: In charge of everything military-related, the Bīngbù deals not only with the recruitment and maintenance of the troops, but also maintains all military buildings, equipment, and supplies. Keeping the ministry well staffed is a requirement if we are to be triumphant in battle.
policies.name: Ministry of War

desc: All the judicial system is managed by the Xíngbù, from petty crimes to the more serious offenses, although it has no authority over the higher spheres of the government. Keeping it in good function will ensure a peaceful society in our realm.
policies.name: Ministry of Justice

desc: Managing all construction in the country, the Gōngbù is in charge of building and maintaining all the infrastructure in our realm, from buildings to roads and canals, as well as the management of resources and the standardization of weights and measures. By ensuring that the ministry works without impediments, the infrastructure of our realm will always have solid foundations.
policies.name: Ministry of Works

desc: The Six Ministries are the distinct administrative divisions of the Middle Kingdom, each one with its own tasks and duties.
entities.name: Six Ministries

desc: The Six Ministries shall report to the Chancellorship represented by the Left and Right Chancellor, the former of whom holds the senior positions.

mods.label: Head of the Cabinet Promotion Cost Modifier

policies.name: Grand Chancellorship

desc: The Six Ministries will pass their paperwork on to the Grand Secretariat, who will conduct analysis and prepare it to be presented to the monarch.
policies.name: Grand Secretariat

desc: The Six Ministries will report directly to the monarch. This strengthens the authority of the monarch, but might also decrease efficiency of rule.
policies.name: Direct Reports

desc: The work of the Six Ministries must be supervised by another agency, or perhaps even the monarch.
entities.name: Six Ministries Supervision

desc: Slaves have been already forced to abandon their homes and live a life of servitude under foreign masters. Let them at least keep their beliefs and rituals; it does not matter what they believe on the inside as long as they obey.
policies.name: Allow Slave Religion

desc: How can we expect slaves to obey and be loyal if they are not willing to embrace our own beliefs, and instead cling to their foolish superstitions? Only by forcing them to abandon their heathenry and accept the true faith wholeheartedly can we ensure their obedience.
policies.name: Force Slave Conversion

desc: Our slaves come from many different lands, and thus bring with them diverse beliefs. We may need to regulate those closely, lest we risk corrupting our own populace by permitting their exposure to deviant practices and rituals.
entities.name: Slave Conversion

desc: Slave trade and slavery are legally allowed throughout our nation.
policies.name: Slave Trade Allowed

desc: Slave trade and slavery are henceforth prohibited throughout our nation.
policies.name: Slave Trade Banned

desc: The influx of workers and cheap labor from external sources has long been a cornerstone of our economy, both at home and abroad. The matter of embracing or banning is a clear reflection of what place the lower strata, and slaves in particular, occupy in our society.
entities.name: Slavery Laws

desc: The Jesuits are a Catholicism religious order, mostly of Iberian origin, that developed along with the Counter-Reformation. Through missionary work and aggressive conversion, their valuable influence and abilities will allow us to accelerate the conversion of our heathen and heretic population at the cost of reduced tolerance.
policies.name: Jesuits Allowed

desc: Despite being able to call upon religious orders to convert our heretic population, we shall instead tolerate all our subjects and treat them as true equals regardless of their beliefs. Jesuit meddling is not welcome in our realm.
policies.name: Not Allowed

desc: The Society of Jesus, commonly known as the Jesuits, is a religious order founded by Ignatius of Loyola as part of the Counter-Reformation. Jesuits are distinguished from other Catholic orders by their emphasis on education, scholarship, and performing missionary work.
entities.name: Society of Jesus

desc: Instead of hanging on the ways of the old, this policy will promote the adaptation of our administration to the expectations of the Han Chinese bureaucrats, who make up many of our statesmen.
policies.name: Promote Chinese Bureaucracy

desc: Due to the overwhelming influence of the Han Chinese, the supremacy of the old Middle Kingdom guard is threatened. They must be expelled from the upper echelons of society.
policies.name: Expel from Bureaucracy

desc: Our dynasty originates from outside the core territory of the Middle Kingdom, making us outsiders to the Han Chinese majority.
entities.name: Status of the Han

desc:
Our state's survival depends on the strength of our warriors. Every male is expected to fight when called upon to do so. To strengthen this warrior culture, the Cihuacōātl is establishing laws that restrict what people may wear, own, and purchase, as well as which government positions each estate may hold, based on their battle prowess.

While these laws protect the rights of our Nobility, they primarily reward martial valor. Among Commoners, combat skill shall determine dress and other privileges. Even Nobility can only access government positions by demonstrating courage in combat.
policies.name: Warrior Culture

desc: Traditions of the past shall be our guiding principles!
policies.name: Tradition

desc:
Clothing in Nahua society reflects our social hierarchy and marks important life events such as marriage, birth, and death. The Commoners typically wear simple cotton garments, while high-ranking elites dress in far more elaborate attire decorated with brilliant colors and priceless feathers. Warriors, by contrast, are permitted to wear only plain mantles.

The Cihuacóatl is now establishing Sumptuary Laws that will regulate how subjects dress, what they may purchase in markets, and which ornaments they may wear, all based on their rank.
entities.name: Sumptuary Law

desc: The traditional tax and currency standard for centuries, Rice, will continue to serve as the basis of our taxation system.
policies.name: Rice-Based Tax

desc: By enacting the Single Whip Policy, we will establish Silver as the basis of our taxation system, enforcing that all financial obligations to the central government are paid in this precious metal.
policies.name: Single Whip Policy

desc: Taxation is the basis of any country's economy. By establishing a proper taxation system throughout the Middle Kingdom, we can more effectively reap the wealth of our territories.
entities.name: Tax Base System

desc: Our people will not be subject to taxation.
policies.name: No Tax Obligations

desc: Our people will pay basic taxes.
policies.name: Fair Tax Obligations

desc: Our people will pay normal taxes, plus additional taxes related to luxury articles.
policies.name: Extensive Tax Obligations

desc: This law defines the level of Taxation that will be applied to our people.
entities.name: Clan Taxation Law

desc: The state reserves itself the exclusive right to manage the Amber resource. The export of this valuable good is managed by government ministers, bolstering the authority of the ruling class.
policies.name: State-Controlled Gathering

desc: It is perhaps best that the Amber is controlled directly by those who trade in it. By eliminating piddling middlemen from the trade process, our overall renevue will greatly expand.
policies.name: Amber in Burghers Hands

desc: Amber should be controlled by the hands that collect it. The resource gathering shall be managed by the Commoners.
policies.name: Gathering by the Commoners

desc: Amber is amongst the most prized resources within our state. Its trade is of ample importance and must be regulated carefully.
entities.name: Amber Monopoly

desc: This state is ruled by the Clergy and uses the hierarchy of religious institutions for all government purposes.
policies.name: Clerical State

desc: This country is ruled by the members of a Monastic Order. The order's hierarchy and rules replace the need for most laws and administration.
policies.name: Monastic Order

desc: A political structure where the nation is governed by a spiritual leader, the Pope, the highest-ranking office of the Catholicism Church.
policies.name: The Papacy

desc: The authority of the Patriarch is the only one that can lead our country, as he is God's maximum representative.
policies.name: Patriarchate

desc: The Caliphate is ruled by the Caliph, the legitimate spiritual successor of the Prophet. Being both the temporal and spiritual higher authority in Islam, all Muslims owe obedience to the Caliph.
policies.name: Caliphate

desc: A Theocratic Leadership governs this country, where religious authorities hold political power and religious law often supersedes secular law.
entities.name: Theocratic Leadership

desc: The sovereignty of the Middle Kingdom and its right to rule shall remain undisputed so long as its divine duty is enforced. All those under Heaven are protected by the Dragon Throne, as various subjects bowing to it.
policies.name: Expand the Tiānxià

desc: Only the direct authority of the Middle Kingdom can be entrusted to rule all under Heaven. The Dragon Throne cannot belittle itself by delegating its authority to lesser countries.
policies.name: Restrict the Tiānxià

desc: The concepts of our territorial influence and expansion are guaranteed by our right to rule, which is granted by Heaven itself.
entities.name: Tiānxià

desc: Trade will be restricted to exchanges between clans.
policies.name: Restricted Clan Trade

desc: Trade will be free for our people.
policies.name: Allow Foreign Exchanges

desc: Trade with China will be allowed.
policies.name: Chinese Tribute

desc: This law sets out constraints for trade partnerships.
entities.name: Trade Relations Law

desc: Workers may partake in collective bargaining and strikes, and protests can be carried out to disrupt production and pressure employers into meeting demands.
policies.name: Allowed

desc: Workers are not allowed to join forces or attempt any collective action. Strikes are illegal.
policies.name: Prohibited

desc: During the early onset of industrialization, trade unions play a crucial role in shaping labor rights and working conditions. These unions negotiate with employers in order to secure better wages, shorter working hours, and safer conditions for their members through collective bargaining.
entities.name: Trade Unions

desc: The lineage of our rulers has been divinely blessed. Their royal blood is what confirms them as worthy of leadership, and therefore we must trust their guidance if we wish to find glory and prosperity.
policies.name: Dynastic Lineage

desc: To ensure a just government, those who hold power in it must be democratically elected. By choosing our leaders, we choose the fate of our nation.
policies.name: Rule by the Public

desc: Allowing mortals to make decisions the fate of our people should not be done without spiritual guidance. Our ruler must be the voice of the gods, and represent their divine judgment in all things.
policies.name: State of Faith

desc: Centralized and formalized states, far from being civilized, are inherently destructive to nature. We must find a different way, and follow the traditional path of balance between the natural and human realms, if we are to truly propser.
policies.name: Tribal Identity

desc: As time progresses, so does our understanding of our culture and identity. We no longer have to fear neighboring tribes; we have tamed the wilderness and have become its master. Now it is time to embrace who we are as a people.
entities.name: Tribal Cultural Identity

desc: There is nothing above the law. It makes the world a more just place, and balances the lives of everyone in our tribe.
policies.name: Codified Power

desc: It is one thing to collaborate in the government of our people — an important, but aseptic task.  It is another thing to share the same food, the same water, the same rituals under the same sun. The customs and ways of our people are something for all of us to share, celebrate, and maintain.
policies.name: Strong Community Customs

desc: The Yassa Decree is the oral law code of the Empire of Mongolia. Publicly declared by Genghis Khān himself, the decree serves as a binding rule within the horde which keeps the government stable and the subjects loyal to their khan.
policies.name: Yassa Decree

desc: Brehon Law is a system of ancient Irish law that developed from pre-Christian customs and traditions. Its unique focus on restitution and compensation, rather than punishment, emphasizes the importance of social harmony and community relationships. However, its lack of formal legal institutions and enforcement mechanisms can lead to inconsistency and uncertainty in its application.
policies.name: Brehon Law

desc: This legal foundation will serve as the basis for the state's first formal code of law. Its goal is simple, yet noble: to secure a just society where all may live in peace and prosperity.
entities.name: Legal Basis

desc: No place can bind us forever, as our spirits are as free as the wind itself. We are entirely nomadic and do not claim any lands as our own.
policies.name: Frequent Migration

desc: As the world changes throughout the year, so must we. Our people cycle through different known sites over the year, returning to the same spots each time. We are as birds, and migrate to find better food, shelter, and breeding opportunities when the seasons turn.
policies.name: Seasonal Travel

desc: Sometimes, following the storm is not as important as finding shelter from it. The time has come for us to establish more permanent settlements that our people can live in all year, every year.
policies.name: Permanent Settlement

desc: Our people do not permanently occupy out lands. Instead, we travel freely, as fate and our people's needs dictate.
entities.name: Tribal Migration

desc: The lineage of our rulers has been divinely blessed. Their royal blood is what confirms them as worthy of leadership, and therefore we must trust their guidance if we wish to find glory and prosperity.
policies.name: Modernize into a Monarchy

desc: To ensure a just government, those who hold power in it must be democratically elected. By choosing our leaders, we choose the fate of our nation.
policies.name: Modernize into a Republic

desc: Allowing mortals to make decisions the fate of our people should not be done without spiritual guidance. Our ruler must be the voice of the gods, and represent their divine judgment in all things.
policies.name: Modernize into a Theocracy

desc: The time has come to discard our old ways and embrace a position in the larger world. No longer seen as a mere tribe, we shall officially become a country, one that represents and defends our people and the way we live.
entities.name: Tribal Modernization

desc: Separation of our people inevitably leads to chaos. Placing all tribal authority under a single chief prevents conflicting directives, ensures clear chains of command, and allows swift, coordinated responses to threats.
policies.name: Centralized Tribe

desc: Together we are stronger. By becoming a Federation, the support that we get from our allies is one not based on diplomacy, but on kinship.
policies.name: Federal Tribe

desc: Trust between the people and their leaders is paramount. By electing a council of members with unquestionable dedication to our interests, we will ensure power is never held by a single person, and that our people's needs are fully met.
policies.name: Clan Council

desc: The tribe is ruled by a council of war chiefs who constantly seek out and recruit skilled fighters for their warbands.
policies.name: Steppe Warbands

desc: A council of noble horse-lords and local clans, this loose administration aims at maintaining our estates and domain, and defending us from rival clans.

mods.label: War with No Casus Belli Cost

policies.name: Jurchen Council

desc: Any group of people requires some form of organization in order to survive and thrive. Tribal organization emphasizes collective identity and customary law, and can be small- or large-scale.
entities.name: Tribal Organization

desc: Our expansion has made us a more diverse and populous community than before. While clan loyalties can take us far, a strongly religious society can better withstand expansion in both time and space, and will give us the cohesion we need to continue growing effectively.
policies.name: Religious Tribe

desc: Religion is undeniably an important aspect of any society. However, it should never threaten the safety and stability of the tribe. As such, we should take a more relaxed view on religion altogether, while still publicly paying respect to spiritual concerns.
policies.name: Lip Service

desc: While religious practices help us maintain our legitimacy, we should not become mired in the principles of righteous rule and morality. Pragmatism will take us further and allow us to support a larger state than slavish spirituality can.
policies.name: Complete Religious Autonomy

desc: The religious values of our tribe dictate not only how we live, but how we treat those who do not share our beliefs and traditions, both within and outside of our territory.
entities.name: Tribal Religious Values

desc: The time to unite our decentralized tribes under a central authority has come! By adopting a more sophisticated social framework, we can make a bid to unite all tribes under our Confederation.
policies.name: Bid for Unification

desc: Every local tribe of the confederation has its own authority, and can make decisions and operate independently.
policies.name: Delegated Authority

desc: States whether the tribes of the Confederation can either act independently, or be forced to submit to a central authority.
entities.name: Unification Law

desc: The succession of the Union is regulated by the laws of the Senior Partner. Each member is forced to adopt these laws if applicable.
policies.name: Unified Succession Law

desc: No member within the Union can determine the legal rights of succession of another member. Each member's policies regarding the throne is a matter of own sovereignty.
policies.name: Sovereign Succession Law

desc: In order to secure the stability of the Union, the inheritance laws of each member must be codified so that each state has the same line of succession.
entities.name: Codified Inheritance

desc: The diplomatic affairs of the Union are centralized in the Senior Partner, while the other members are limited in their foreign diplomacy. The matters of warfare, however, are still in the hands of the Estates, even though now they are significantly more incentivized to take less risks in their endeavors.

mods.label: Allow Enforce Union Peace in Union

policies.name: Unified External Diplomacy

desc: The diplomats of the Union serve no singular banner, but the entirety of the Union. Each member has access to their abilities and can utilize them for their own foreign affairs.
policies.name: Organized Diplomats

desc:
As the Union is led from a single throne, so comes the question of how the diplomacy of the Union shall be handled.

The matters of warfare, though, are nonetheless in the hands of the Estates of our union partners.
entities.name: Diplomatic Liberties

desc: The different treasuries of the Union shall be unified into one single entity which fills the coffers of the monarch and allows them to spend the gold in the best interest of the Union.
policies.name: Unified Treasury

desc: The treasuries of the members of the Union serve nobody exclusively. They are part of the royal commune, and shall be used to improve the infrastructure of every member.
policies.name: Cooperative Investment

desc: One monarch might rule over multiple thrones, yet the members of the Union are very separated in their economy. This law shall bring all of them closer to each other.
entities.name: Economy of the Union

desc: The Union can only hold together from a single throne. Designating the senior partner of the Union shall also determine which throne shall represent the Union as a whole.
policies.name: Establish Seniority

desc: The sovereignty of each member of the Union is untouchable and unquestionable. Even if each throne is ruled by a single ruler, it is not the monarch's business to meddle in the affairs of the union members.
policies.name: Maintain Federal Status

desc: The law of the Union which determines its very nature and if it should follow a centralized or federal future - if it can stand the test of time.
entities.name: Union Foundation

desc: In order to keep administrative cohesion and consistency within the Union, all laws and policies shall be aligned with the ones of the Senior Partner.
policies.name: Aligned Legislature

desc: Differences in customs and laws are no flaw but a primary aspect of the different members of the Union. As such, the design of policies is an untouchable responsibility of the member states instead of the ruler.
policies.name: Federal Legislature

desc: The adminstration of the Union requires a cohesive design. An approved, unitary system of a legislature is imperative to ensure the stability of the Union.
entities.name: Legislature of the Union

desc: The Union serves as an aggressive alliance. Enemies shall tremble as our soldiers move in unity against them.
policies.name: Assured Offense

desc: The Union has a strong aggressive nature to it. Every member is appealed to follow their fellow members to the offensive war.
policies.name: Duty for Offense

desc: In order to survive, the Union must thrive through conquest and growth of their own power. Each member may be allowed to call in other members in times of war.
policies.name: Possible Offense

desc: Although first and foremost defensive in its nature, the military might of a Union can be called to support each other in military campaigns - if the state members agree to such obligation.
entities.name: Mutual Offense

desc: Further improvements in the different parts of the bureaucracy of the Senior Partner have led to an optimization of the annexation process of the Junior Partner.
policies.name: Rapid Unification of Crowns

desc: The diplomatic and administrative bureaucracy within the Senior Partner has been improved greatly, allowing for a quicker integration of the member states.
policies.name: Swift Unification of Crowns

desc: The time has come to centralize the Union at last! Under the graceful watch of the Senior Partner, the member states have agreed to processes of diplomatic annexation.
policies.name: Unification of Crowns

desc: The Union is first and foremost a defensive alliance. No member state is interested in unifying the thrones into a single political entity, and the sovereignty of the each individual state is protected.
policies.name: Federal Union

desc: The Union is in its most variations nothing but a loose confederation of different states ruled from the same throne. However, the possibility of a unification under the banner of the Senior Partner is not out of question...
entities.name: Question of Unification

desc: Vajrayāna, also called Tantric Buddhism or Esoteric Buddhism, is a form of Buddhism that incorporates many tantric, esoteric, and ritualistic practices. Its development has been strongly influenced by other religions, especially Hinduism.
policies.name: Tantric Practices

desc: Vajrayāna, also called Tantric Buddhism or Esoteric Buddhism, is a form of Buddhism that incorporates many tantric, esoteric, and ritualistic practices. Its development has been strongly influenced by other religions, especially Hinduism.
entities.name: Tantric Practices

desc: In Venice, loyalty to the Republic is more important than what type of Christianity you are.
policies.name: Venetian First, Christianity Second

desc: Being a proper Christianity is the only thing that matters for a citizen of Venice.
policies.name: Christianity First!

desc: The Holy Office has been requesting greater jurisdiction over religious life in the Most Serene Republic. We must now choose whether to comply with this request, or to defend the religious freedom of our subjects.
entities.name: The Holy Office

desc: Items are categorized according to their practical and symbolic significance, as their intended use is lavish state ceremonies to impress foreign dignitaries and diplomatic gifts.
policies.name: Diplomatic Focus

desc: Items are managed according to their usefulness to governance and financial planning so that they can be efficiently used for building projects, and ensure that government expenditures are kept under control.
policies.name: Administrative Focus
